SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.claim: The preceding verse begins by honoring humanity through creation of the earth’s contents for people and ends by affirming God’s knowledge; Adam’s story develops both themes.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r2.anchor: بدأت بتكريم الإنسان: {خَلَقَ لَكُمْ مَّا فِي الأرض جَمِيعاً} وختمت بالعلم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.claim: Successful vicegerency requires authority to manage the entrusted domain and the capacity and knowledge to do so; the preceding verse summarizes both through creation of the earth for people and God's knowledge.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/r5.anchor: الاستخلاف الناجح لا بد أن يتم له أمران: الأول: أن يكون للخليفة حَقُّ التصرف والتدبير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p841/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p841/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p841/r5.claim: السماوات reflects the general early script, which omitted weak letters; the scribes followed the contemporary writing system rather than inventing a special Qur’anic script.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p841/r5.anchor: حين كُتب القرآن كان حرف العلة (الواو، الألف والياء) لا يُرسم هذا كاتجاه عام ثم تغيّر الخط لاحقاً فأصبحت حروف العلة تُرسم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r1.claim: Thumma orders the presentation of statements, not events themselves. One view says istawā means rose without specifying how or delimiting God; al-Ṭabarī prefers this, glossing it as the rule of His command, power, and dominion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r1.anchor: معناه علا دون تكييف ولا تحديد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysān glosses istawā as turning toward heaven; Ibn ʿAṭiyya specifies that this means turning to create and originate it.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r3.claim: Some say God completed heaven's construction, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls that interpretation strained; al-Ṭabarī also reports “turned toward” as a weak option.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r4.claim: The report that the subject of “the one who rose” is smoke conflicts with the wording's arrangement, while interpreting istawā as “conquered” fits 20:5 better; here one retains God's power and dominion without movement or created change.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r4.anchor: والقاعدة في هذه الآية ونحوها منع النقلة وحلول الحوادث

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r5.claim: Fasawwāhunna can mean making the heavens equal or smoothing their surfaces; sabʿa may be apposition, object with an understood preposition, or circumstantial, and al-samāʾ can be plural or a collective singular.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r6.claim: God's knowledge encompasses existing things; knowledge of nonexistents is established by other verses. Earth was created before heaven, then spread out afterward, reconciling this verse with passages in al-Muʾmin and al-Nāziʿāt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p115/r6.anchor: وهذه الآية تقتضي أن الأرض وما فيها خلق قبل السماء

THALABI:v1p173/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p173/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v1p173/r10.claim: God created all earthly things for people, then directed Himself to creating seven even heavens, without gaps, fractures, supporting pillars, or signs above them; He knows everything.
THALABI:v1p173/r10.anchor: ما في الأرض جميعا ثم استوى إلى السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r11.claim: استواء means straightness and balance; استوى إليه can mean proceeding toward something directly, while تسوية means leveling and adjusting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p192#2/r11.anchor: الاستواء: الاعتدال والاستقامة، استوى العود وغيره: إذا استقام واعتدل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r1.claim: The lām in “for you” can denote cause and benefit, ownership or permission, or a broader relation of particularity; the preferred reading is purpose and benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r1.anchor: والأحسن حملها على السبب فيكون مفعولا من أجله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r2.claim: Creation benefits people religiously through reflection on its design and the afterlife, and materially through food, drink, clothing, marriage, transport, and scenery.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r3.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r3.claim: Some use “created for you” to argue that things are presumptively permitted before revealed law.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r3.anchor: وقد استدل بقوله: خلق لكم، من ذهب إلى أن الأشياء قبل ورود الشرع على الإباحة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r4.claim: Because the lām may mean something other than ownership or permission, this verse alone does not prove the presumption of permissibility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r4.anchor: وإذا احتمل أن يكون اللام لغير التمليك والإباحة، لم يكن في ذلك دليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r5.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r5.claim: Others hold that things are forbidden until law permits them, so one should not act without authorization.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r5.anchor: وقد ذهب قوم إلى أن الأشياء قبل ورود الشرع على الحظر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r6.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r6.claim: A third group suspends judgment because they see arguments for both initial permissibility and prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r6.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن الوقف لنا تعارض عندهم دليل القائلين بالإباحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r7.speaker: أبو بكر بن فورك عن ابن الصائغ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r7.claim: Ibn al-Sa'igh is reported to say reason has never lacked transmitted guidance: every case has a text, a precedent, or a continuing prior ruling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r7.anchor: وحكى أبو بكر بن فورك عن ابن الصائغ أنه قال: لم يخل العقل قط من السمع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r8.claim: “All that is on earth” includes animals, plants, minerals, mountains, and things produced through human crafts and derived processes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r8.anchor: واندرج تحت قوله: ما في الأرض جميعا، جميع ما كانت الأرض مستقرا له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r9.claim: Some infer that clay is forbidden because the verse grants what is on earth, not the earth itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r9.anchor: واستدل بعضهم بذلك على تحريم الطين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r10.claim: Together with the earlier blessing that earth was made a resting place, this verse’s blessing for its contents implies that God made both earth and its contents for people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r10.anchor: وقد تقدم قبل هذا الامتنان بجعل الأرض لنا فراشا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r11.claim: The accusative jamiʿan is a confirmatory circumstantial qualifier of the created things; it means the whole, like kull, not simultaneous existence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r11.anchor: وانتصب جميعا على الحال من المخلوق، وهي حال مؤكدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r12.claim: Taking “what is on earth” to mean the earth and everything in it is distant from the phrase’s literal scope, though it paraphrases its contextual meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p215/r12.anchor: ومن زعم أن المعني بقوله: ما في الأرض، الأرض وما فيها، فهو بعيد عن مدلول اللفظ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows “earth” to mean the lower regions, just as “heaven” can mean the upper regions; the ground and its contents are included below.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r1.anchor: إن أراد بالأرض الجهات السفلية دون الغبراء، كما تذكر السماء، ويراد بها الجهات العلوية، جاز ذلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r2.speaker: بعض المنسوبين للحقائق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r2.claim: Some mystical writers read “created for you” as an enumeration of blessings that should prompt gratitude and seeking further gifts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r2.anchor: خلق لكم ليعد نعمه عليكم، فتقتضي الشكر من نفسك لتطلب المزيد منه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r3.claim: Abu Uthman says God gave and subjected everything to reveal His generosity, reassure people about the afterlife, and show that great gifts exceed little deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r3.anchor: وهب لك الكل وسخره لك لتستدل به على سعة جوده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r4.claim: Ibn Ata says the whole universe is yours while you are for God; do not let what is yours distract you from Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r4.anchor: خلق لكم ليكون الكون كله لك وتكون لله فلا تشتغل بما لك عما أنت له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r5.speaker: بعض البغداديين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r5.claim: Some Baghdadi mystics say blessings make people worship blessings; when a person encounters God, the Benefactor hides the blessings from view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r5.anchor: أنعم عليك بها، فإن الخلق عبدة النعم لاستيلاء النعم عليهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r6.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r6.claim: Al-Thawri describes severance from attachments as the highest station of the people of spiritual realization.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r6.anchor: الثوري: أعلى مقامات أهل الحقائق الانقطاع عن العلائق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r7.claim: The particle thumma ordinarily signals temporal delay, although time did not yet exist when the heavens were made.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r7.anchor: والعطف بثم يقتضي التراخي في الزمان، ولا زمان إذ ذاك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r8.claim: One explanation makes thumma signal the difference in magnitude between creating earth and creating the heavens, rather than temporal delay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r8.anchor: فقيل: أشار بثم إلى التفاوت الحاصل بين خلق السماء والأرض في القدر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r9.claim: Another explanation allows an interval for making mountains, blessing earth, and apportioning its provisions before turning to heaven.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r9.anchor:
وقيل:
لما كان بين خلق الأرض والسماء أعمال من جعل الرواسي والبركة فيها وتقدير الأقوات عطف بثم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r10.claim: The word istawā is read with fatḥ by the Hijazis and imāla by Najdis; both forms occur among the seven canonical readers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r10.anchor: استوى أهل الحجاز على الفتح، ونجد على الإمالة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r11.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r11.claim: Al-Farra interprets istawā ilayh as turning deliberately to create heaven, like an arrow sent straight at its target; al-Zamakhshari chooses this metaphor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r11.anchor: أقبل وعمد إلى خلقها وقصد من غير أن يريد فيما بين ذلك خلق شيء آخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r12.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r12.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas interprets istiwāʾ as rising without specifying how or setting limits, understood as the rise of God’s command and authority; al-Tabari prefers it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r12.anchor: علا وارتفع من غير تكييف ولا تحديد، قاله الربيع بن أنس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r13.claim: A third interpretation takes ilā as ʿalā, meaning God alone held sovereignty over heaven rather than making it the property of creation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r13.anchor: أن يكون إلى بمعنى على، أي استوى على السماء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r14.speaker: شاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p216/r14.claim: Abu Hayyan introduces a poetic illustration for the reading of istawā as sovereign control over heaven.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r1.speaker: الحسن البصري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r1.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri interprets the phrase as God’s command turning toward and settling in heaven; “command” is understood as an omitted noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r1.anchor: تحول أمره إلى السماء واستقر فيها، والاستواء هو الاستقرار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysan explains it as God’s making and fashioning heaven, a meaning that returns to the first interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r2.anchor: أن المعنى استوى بخلقه واختراعه إلى السماء، قاله ابن كيسان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r3.claim: A sixth interpretation glosses istawā as completing the work in heaven, but Abu Hayyan says the wording does not support it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r3.anchor:
السادس:
أن المعنى كمل صنعه فيها، كما تقول: استوى الأمر، وهذا ينبو اللفظ عن الدلالة عليه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r4.claim: A seventh, very remote interpretation makes the pronoun in istawā refer to the smoke, which clashes with the context and pronouns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r4.anchor: السابع: أن الضمير في استوى عائد على الدخان، وهذا بعيد جدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r5.claim: All these interpretations avoid attributing ordinary movement or change to God, or saying that God enters or is entered by something created.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r5.anchor: وهذه التأويلات كلها فرار عما تقرر في العقول من أن الله تعالى يستحيل أن يتصف بالانتقال المعهود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r6.claim: Taswiyah can mean proportioning and straightening the heavens, completing their creation, making them equal, or smoothing their surfaces.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r6.anchor: ومعنى التسوية: تعديل خلقهن وتقويمه وإحلاؤه من العوج والفطور،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r7.claim: The feminine plural pronoun in fasawwāhunna can refer to heaven as a collective noun or to the singular generic “heaven” intended here as plural.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r7.anchor: والضمير في فسواهن عائد على السماء على أنها جمع سماوة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls the pronoun ambiguous and treats “seven heavens” as its explanation, comparing it to the construction “he raised him a man.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r8.anchor: والضمير في فسواهن ضمير مبهم. وسبع سماوات تفسيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r9.claim: Abu Hayyan says this is not one of the established Arabic types of indefinite pronouns and weakens the connection to the preceding clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p217/r9.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره الزمخشري ليس واحدا من هذه الضمائر التي سردناها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r1.claim: Making “seven heavens” an apposition to the preceding pronoun is grammatically sound, as in “your brother, I passed by him, Zayd.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r1.anchor: وقد أعرب بعضهم سبع سموات بدلا من الضمير على أن الضمير عائد على ما قبله، وهو إعراب صحيح،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r2.claim: Parsing “seven heavens” as a direct object with an omitted preposition is poor: سوى does not behave like اختار, and the reading implies more than seven heavens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r2.anchor: وهذا ليس بجيد من حيث اللفظ ومن حيث المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r3.claim: Parsing it as a second object meaning “made into” is poor because سوى normally takes one object and is not established with the meaning “make.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r3.anchor: وهذا ليس بجيد، لأن تعدي سوى لواحد هو المعلوم في اللغة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r4.claim: A circumstantial qualifier is also possible, but apposition is stronger because the pronoun refers back to the previous noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r4.anchor: والمختار البدل باعتبار عود الضمير على ما قبله والحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r5.claim: Scholars disagree whether heaven or earth was created first, each citing the apparent sense of other verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r5.anchor: وقد اختلف أهل العلم في أيهما خلق قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r6.claim: Abu Hayyan reads this verse as placing the creation of earthly things before the sevenfold shaping of heaven; earth’s body came first, then it was spread after heaven, reconciling the verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r6.anchor: والمختار أن جرم الأرض خلق قبل السماء، وخلقت السماء بعدها، ثم دحيت الأرض بعد خلق السماء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r7.claim: Some explain the number seven as expressing intensified power and force, since Arabs use seven and seventy for emphatic doubling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r7.anchor: لأن السبعة والسبعين فيه دلالة على تضاعيف القوة والشدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r8.claim: Seven also marks major things in Arab usage: days, heavens, earths, the visible planets, seas, and the gates of Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r8.anchor: والسبعة تذكر في جلائل الأمور: الأيام سبعة، والسموات سبع، والأرض سبع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r9.claim: The hāʾ of huwa and hiya may be made still after wāw, fa, lām, and thumma; it is less common after kāf and interrogative hamza and rare after lakin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r9.anchor: وتسكين الهاء في هو وهي بعد الواو والفاء واللام وثم جائز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r10.speaker: أبو حمدون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r10.claim: Abu Hamdun has a rare reading with a still hāʾ in “lakin huwa rabbī,” compared to syllable-smoothing in words such as sabʿ and karish.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p218/r10.anchor: وندر بعد لكن، في قراءة أبي حمدون، لكن هو الله ربي،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي وقالون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r1.claim: Abu Amr, al-Kisai, and Qalun read huwa with a still hāʾ; the other readers retain the original vowel, and Yaqub pauses with an added hāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r1.anchor: وقرأ بتسكين وهو أبو عمرو والكسائي وقالون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r2.claim: In “knowing everything,” the intensive form ʿalīm governs “everything”; grammar would ordinarily use a preposition when that complement comes first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r2.anchor: وكان القياس التعدي باللام حالة التقديم، أو بنفسه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r3.claim: Intensive forms preserve the preposition of verbs that take one; with knowledge or ignorance they use bi-, while other direct-object verbs take li-, resembling the elative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r3.anchor: إن كان متعديا بحرف جر تعدى المثال بحرف الجر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r4.claim: When an intensive form appears to govern a direct object after it, grammarians analyze that object as governed by an omitted verb indicated by the elative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r4.anchor: أول بأنه معمول لفعل محذوف يدل عليه أفعل التفضيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r5.claim: If “thing” includes both existent and nonexistent entities, this verse directly shows God knows both; if it means only existing things, another proof establishes knowledge of nonexistents.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r5.anchor: فمن أطلقه على الموجود والمعدوم كان تعلق العلم بهما من هذه الآية ظاهرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r6.claim: ʿAlīm is an intensive form, as are ʿālim and ʿallām; Arabs add tāʾ in ʿallāma for emphasis, but that form is not used of God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r6.anchor: وقد وصف تعالى نفسه بعالم وعليم وعلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r7.claim: Divine intensification reflects the vast range of known things, not multiple acts of knowledge: God’s single knowledge encompasses every whole and detail, subtle and great, existent and nonexistent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r7.anchor: لأن علمه تعالى واحد لا تكثير فيه، فلما تعلق علمه تعالى بالجميع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r8.claim: The closing description “knowing” suits the account of creation and control of the upper and lower worlds, death, and life, all of which display complete knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r8.anchor: وناسب مقطع هذه الآية بالوصف بمبالغة العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r9.claim: The claim that ʿalīm means knowledge from oneself while ʿālim means knowledge acquired from another is false, since God calls Himself ʿālim without learning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p219/r9.anchor: وهذا ليس بجيد لأن الله تعالى قد وصف نفسه بالعالم، ولم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r1.claim: The universal wording “knowing everything” rejects the claim that God knows universals but not particulars.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r1.anchor: وفي تعميم قوله تعالى: بكل شيء عليم رد على من زعم أن علم الله تعالى متعلق بالكليات لا بالجزئيات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r2.claim: Divine knowledge is one, unchanging, not gained through sense or thought, necessary and unable to cease, never distracted, and encompasses infinitely many objects.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r2.anchor: علم الله تعالى يتميز على علم عباده بكونه واحدا يعلم به جميع المعلومات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r6.claim: After warning comes remembrance of blessings in earth, heaven, and useful creation, joining threat with encouragement as sound-minded moral instruction.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r6.anchor: ثم بعد التخويف ذكرهم تعالى بنعمه التي أنعمها عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r7.claim: The section ends by declaring God’s knowledge encompasses everything from beginning to end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p221/r7.anchor: ثم ختم ذلك بالفصل الأكبر من إعلامهم بإحاطة علمه بجميع الأشياء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.claim: The phrase about being dead, then made alive, dying, and being revived can be attached to an implied command to remember these events; the beginning already lets the thoughtful infer the return.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r1.anchor: إذ من البدءة تعلم العودة لمن تدبر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.claim: Humanity was made for lasting life, not extinction: God created the cosmos for people, as provision, means, and support for their preservation and development.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83#2/r2.anchor: لم يخلق هذا النوع البشري للفناء بل للبقاء

ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r4.claim: Provision is not confined to Earth: its most important basis is in heaven, and al-Baqara 2:29 also directs attention to heaven after creation of what is on Earth.
ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r4.anchor: rızkımızın en mühim esası semâda olmasına

ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r5.claim: As people walk Earth, they also travel toward heaven, receiving air, light, and other material and spiritual descents through known and unknown means.
ELMALILI:67:15-19#3/r5.anchor: Arz’ın omuzlarında yürürken yalnız Arz’da değil, onunla beraber semâya doğru da

SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r1.claim: هو is a detached masculine nominative pronoun serving as the subject, and the following relative clause is its predicate; its wāw is usually light and fatḥa, but can also be geminated, quiescent or omitted in poetry.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r1.anchor: هو مبتدأ وهو ضمير مرفوع منفصل للغائب المذكر، والمشهور تخفيف واوه وفتحها، وقد تشدد

SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r2.claim: لكم with خلق can mean causal benefit, for your sake; alternatively ownership or permissive use, limited to beneficial things, or اختصاص.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r2.anchor: و " لكم " متعلق بخلق، ومعناه السببية، أي: لأجلكم، وقيل: للملك والإباحة

SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r3.claim: ما is a relative pronoun, في الأرض its relative clause, and the whole is the direct object of خلق.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r3.anchor: و " ما " موصولة و " في الأرض " صلتها، وهي في محل نصب مفعول بها

SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r4.claim: جميعا is a circumstantial accusative meaning all and does not imply simultaneous creation, unlike معا, which implies shared timing; it may be emphatic since ما في الأرض is already general.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29/r4.anchor: و " جميعا " حال من المفعول بمعنى كل، ولا دلالة لها على الاجتماع في الزمان

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r1.claim: Since ثم usually marks temporal delay and no interval is intended by one view, it signals delay in rank between creating earth and heaven; another allows time for intervening acts such as making mountains and apportioning provisions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r1.anchor: فقيل: إشارة إلى التراخي بين رتبتي خلق الأرض والسماء

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r2.claim: استوى can mean became straight and balanced, or rose and ascended; the author cites poetry and المؤمنون 23:28 for usage.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r2.anchor: واستوى معناه لغة: استقام واعتدل، من استوى العود. وقيل: علا وارتفع

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r3.claim: The subject of استوى refers to God. Ibn Atiyya's proposal that it refers to smoke is rejected because no antecedent signals it and the wording says He turned to the heaven, which is smoke.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r3.anchor: وفاعل استوى ضمير يعود على الله، وقيل: يعود على الدخان نقله ابن عطية

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r4.claim: إلى normally marks an endpoint; another view reads it as على and takes استوى as استولى, supported by poetry about Bishr over Iraq and another poem.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r4.anchor: و " إلى " حرف انتهاء على بابها، وقيل: هي بمعنى " على " فيكون في المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r5.claim: An alternative supplies an omitted subject noun: استوى أمره, with أمره as the subject of استوى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: ثم مضاف محذوف، ضميره هو الفاعل أي استوى أمره

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r6.claim: The feminine pronoun refers to السماء, either because its underlying form سماوة is collective or because السماء is a collective noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r6.anchor: و " فسواهن " الضمير يعود على السماء: إما لأنها جمع سماوة كما تقدم

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls هن an ambiguous pronoun explained by سبع سماوات, like ربه رجلا; a critic says explained pronouns are limited to listed constructions, perhaps admitting apposition here.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r7.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " هن " ضمير مبهم، و " سبع سماوات " يفسره كقولهم: " ربه رجلا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r8.claim: The author says an apposition analysis weakens the connection to the previous clause and makes two independent reports; the apparent sense is that what God approached is what He fashioned.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#2/r8.anchor: لكن هذا يضعف بكون هذا التقدير يجعله غير مرتبط بما قبله ارتباطا كليا

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r1.claim: The strongest of five parses makes سبع سماوات apposition to the pronoun in فسواهن, which refers to السماء.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r1.anchor: أحسنها: أنه بدل من الضمير في { فسواهن } العائد على السماء

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r2.claim: A second parse also makes it apposition to the pronoun, but says that the pronoun is explained by what follows; this is weakened by the earlier objection to al-Zamakhshari's account.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r2.anchor: الثاني: أنه بدل من الضمير أيضا، ولكن هذا الضمير يفسره ما بعده

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa and others take it as an object with an elided من, as if فسوى منهن سبع سماوات, by analogy with 7:155; the author rejects this because the verb pattern does not allow it and it implies more heavens from which seven were chosen.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r3.anchor: قاله أبو البقاء وغيره. وهذا ضعيف لوجهين، أحدهما بالنسبة إلى اللفظ

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r4.claim: A fourth parse makes سوى mean صير and سبع a second object; the author says this meaning of سوى is unestablished.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r4.anchor: الرابع: أن " سوى " بمعنى صير فيتعدى لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r5.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash allows a fifth parse as a circumstantial accusative, but it is remote because it is prospective and requires an adjective-like interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#3/r5.anchor: الخامس: أن ينتصب حالا ويعزى للأخفش. وفيه بعد من وجهين

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r1.claim: هو is the subject, عليم its predicate, and the preceding prepositional phrase attaches to عليم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r1.anchor: " هو " مبتدأ و " عليم " خبره، والجار قبله يتعلق به

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r2.claim: The هاء of هو and هي may be quiescent after wāw, fāʾ, lam of emphasis or ثم; frequent adjacency lets a detached pronoun behave like a connected form, as in the cited verses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r2.anchor: يجوز تسكين هاء " هو " و " هي " بعد الواو والفاء ولام الابتداء وثم

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r3.claim: Quiescent هاء in هو is also attested after ك, after interrogative hamza, and after لكن in Ibn Hamdun's reading at 18:38; the text also cites يمل هو in 2:282.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r3.anchor: وقد تسكن بعد كاف الجر كقوله: 325 فقلت لهم ما هن كهي فكيف لي

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r4.claim: Intensive forms differ from their verbs and active participles because they resemble elatives in intensified meaning and therefore take the elative's patterns of government.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r4.anchor: أن أمثلة المبالغة خالفت أفعالها وأسماء فاعليها لمعنى وهو شبهها بأفعل التفضيل

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r5.claim: Intensive forms based on directly transitive verbs of knowing or ignorance take ب, as in أعلم بكم, عليم بذات الصدور and جهول بك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r5.anchor: فإن كان الأول: فإما أن يفهم علما أو جهلا أو لا، فإن كان الأول تعدت بالباء نحو

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r6.claim: Other intensive forms from directly transitive verbs take ل, as in أضرب لزيد and له ضراب; the source also cites فعال لما يريد.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r6.anchor: وإن كان الثاني تعدت باللام نحو: أنا أضرب لزيد منك وأنا له ضراب

SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r7.claim: If the base verb governs through a preposition, its intensive form keeps that preposition, as in صبور عليه and زهيد فيه.
SAMIN-DURR:2:29#4/r7.anchor: وإن كانت من متعد بحرف جر تعدت هي بذلك الحرف نحو: أنا أصبر على كذا

ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r6.claim: Mā is the object: everything on earth is created as a benefit bestowed for you.
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r6.anchor: موضع ما مفعول به وتأويله أن جميع ما في الأرض منعم به عليكم فهو لكم.

ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r7.claim: An alternative explanation takes provision of everything on earth as evidence for God’s oneness.
ZAJJAJ:v1p106/r7.anchor: وفيه قول آخر أن ذلكم دليل على توحيد الله عز وجل.

ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r1.claim: Some understand istawā ilā as intending or turning toward heaven, as a prince is said to turn toward a city.
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r1.anchor: فيه قولان: قال بعضهم: (استوى إلى السماء)، عمد وقصد إلى السماء.

ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as God’s command ascending to heaven.
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r2.anchor: وقد قيل (أيضا) استوى أي صعد أمره إلى السماء وهذا قول ابن عباس،

ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r3.claim: Al-samāʾ has singular form but plural meaning, as shown by the phrase ‘made them seven heavens.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r3.anchor: والسماء لفظها لفظ الواحد، ومعناها معنى الجمع. والدليل على ذلك قوله: (فسواهن سبع سماوات).

ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r4.claim: Alternatively, al-samāʾ may itself be a plural, with singular forms samāh or samāwah and samāʾ used for the collective.
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون السماء جمعا كما أن السماوات جمع كأن واحده سماة وسماوة وسماء للجميع.

ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash allows a singular form such as al-samāʾ to denote a plural, as in ‘the dirham and dinar became numerous among people.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r5.anchor: وزعم أبو الحسن الأخفش أن السماء جائز أن يكون واحدا يراد به الجمع

ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r6.claim: The word means a roof and more generally anything elevated; clouds are called sky because they are high.
ZAJJAJ:v1p107/r6.anchor: والسماء في اللغة السقف ويقال لكل ما ارتفع وعلا قد سما يسمو، وكل سقف، فهو سماء

ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r1.claim: Samaʾ means anything spread like a canopy above another thing; it primarily denotes the visible skies in the Qur’an and more broadly a cosmic system.
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r1.anchor: anything that is spread like a canopy above any other thing

ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r2.claim: In Arabic and apparently other Semitic usage, seven can mean several, while seventy or seven hundred can mean many or very many; Asad cites Lisan al-ʿArab and Taj al-ʿArus.
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r2.anchor: in Arabic usage - and apparently in other Semitic languages as well - the number "seven" is often synonymous with "several"

ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r3.claim: Combining that usage with Raghib’s definition of each heaven relative to what is below it, Asad reads “seven heavens” as multiple cosmic systems.
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r3.anchor: every sama' is a sama' with regard to what is below it" (Raghib)

ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r4.claim: Asad renders thumma as “and” at the start of this sentence and refers readers to his note on surah 7.
ASAD-NOTES:2:29#n20/r4.anchor: For my rendering of thumma, at the beginning of this sentence, as "and", see surah 7, first part of note 43.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r3.claim: Some read the pronoun hāʾ with sukūn after wāw, fa, thumma, and lām; connection to these particles lightens it, as with the imperative lām.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r3.anchor: يقرأ باسكان الهاء مع الواو والفاء وثم واللام وبحركتها بالضم فالحجة لمن اسكن أنه لما اتصلت هذه الهاء بهذه الحروف أسكنت تخفيفا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r4.claim: Other readers retain ḍamma on hāʾ, preserving the pronoun's original form before the particles.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r4.anchor: والحجة لمن ضم أنه أتى بلفظ الاسم على أصله قبل دخوله هذه الحروف عليه

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r5.speaker: بعض القراء
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r5.claim: Some readers use sukūn with particles that cannot be paused after, but retain the vowel when pausing is possible, since the following noun then stands independently.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p73#2/r5.anchor: وقد فرق بعض القراء بين هذه الحروف فأسكن مع ما لا يوقف عليه منها وحرك ما يوقف عليه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r2.speaker: ابن كثير، عاصم، ابن عامر، حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r2.claim: These readers vocalize the hāʾ in huwa and related forms after wāw, fāʾ, lām, or thumma; al-Kisāʾī leaves it still.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر وحمزة ﴿ وهو ﴾ ﴿ فهو ﴾ ولهو وثم هو وهي ﴿ فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا ﴾ الفرقان 5 بتحريك الهاء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r3.speaker: الكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads these hāʾs with sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r3.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بتخفيف ذلك وإسكان الهاء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r5.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r5.speaker: نافع: ابن جماز، أبو بكر بن أبي أويس، ورش
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r5.claim: These transmitters report vocalization from Nāfiʿ throughout the forms under discussion.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r5.anchor: فروى ابن جماز وأبو بكر بن أبي أويس وورش وأخبرني محمد بن الفرج عن ابن المسيب عن أبيه عن نافع التثقيل في ذلك كله

IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r6.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r6.speaker: نافع: قالون، إسماعيل بن أبي أويس، خلف، ابن سعدان عن إسحق
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r6.claim: These transmitters report sukūn throughout; Abū ʿUbayd transmits the same from Ismāʿīl.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p151/r6.anchor: وروى قالون وإسماعيل بن أبي أويس وخلف وابن سعدان عن إسحق عن نافع التخفيف في كل ذلك

QIRAAT-ER:2:29:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:29:3#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:29:3#1/r1.claim: The standard reading is the Form I perfect active verb khalaqa.
QIRAAT-ER:2:29:3#1/r1.anchor: Standard reading: Form I perfect active.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says the earth was created before the heaven; smoke rose from it, after which God formed seven heavens, one above another, and seven earths, one below another.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ثم استوى إلى السماء ﴾ قال خلق الأرض قبل السماء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r2.claim: Qatada says the seven heavens lie one above another, with a journey of five hundred years between each pair.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p41#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ فسواهن سبع سماوات ﴾ قال بعضهن فوق بعض بين كل سماءين مسيرة خمسمائة عام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r6.claim: After recalling creation, death, and resurrection into Paradise or Fire, the passage argues that God deserves worship; it then recalls His earthly gifts, heavenly power, and knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r6.anchor: هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا: مناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها ظاهرة، وهو أنه لما ذكر أن من كان منشئا لكم بعد العدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r7.claim: Huwa is the masculine singular third-person pronoun; in use it can refer to any absent masculine singular, with its referent fixed when a predicate is assigned.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r7.anchor: ولفظة هو من المضمرات وضع للمفرد المذكر الغائب، وهو كلي في الوضع كسائر المضمرات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r8.claim: Arab dialects commonly lighten the wāw with fatḥa; Hamdān geminates it, Asad and Qays make it still, and poetic usage alone deletes it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v1p213/r8.anchor: ومشهور لغات العرب تخفيف الواو مفتوحة، وشددتها همدان، وسكنتها أسد وقيس، وحذف الواو مختص بالشعر.

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r1.claim: The creation clause joins the preceding account without a conjunction, either as its result or to mark that it independently conveys its point; it announces another blessing dependent on the first because benefit requires life.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r1.anchor: معطوف على قوله تعالى ﴿ وكنتم ﴾ وترك الحرف إما لكونه كالنتيجة له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r2.claim: God made everything on earth for people’s benefit: directly or indirectly in worldly affairs, and in religious affairs through inference and reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r2.anchor: خلق لأجلكم جميع ما في الأرض لتنتفعوا به في أمور دنياكم بالذات أو بالواسطة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r3.claim: هو is a third-person pronoun with dialectal forms: its wāw may be lightened or omitted in poetry, doubled in Himyar, and quiescent in Asad and Qays.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r3.anchor: لغير المتكلم والمخاطب وفيه لغات تخفيف الواو مفتوحة وحذفها في الشعر وتشديدها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r4.speaker: أهل الله
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r4.claim: The people of God treat هو as a divine name indicating the uniquely specified essence, free of every kind of multiplicity.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r4.anchor: عند أهل الله تعالى اسم من أسمائه تعالى ينبىء عن كنه حقيقته المخصوصة المبرأة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r5.claim: One mystical-linguistic account makes هو a two-letter compound whose hāʾ is original and wāw extra; because wāw drops in dual and plural, it ultimately signals the one, sole existent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r5.anchor: اسم مركب من حرفين الهاء والواو والهاء أصل والواو زائدة بدليل سقوطها في التثنية والجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r6.claim: The same account says spiritual elders made هو the center of remembrance and lamp of the inward secret, repeated with each breath, while its referent eludes perception and analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r6.anchor: ولمزيد ما فيه من الأسرار اتخذه الأجلة مدارا لذكرهم وسراجا لسرهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r7.claim: Making the pronoun the subject and the relative phrase its predicate itself signals God’s majesty; putting “for you” before the direct object hastens the glad tidings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r7.anchor: الضمير مبتدأ والموصول خبرا من الدلالة على الجلالة ما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r8.claim: Many Sunnī Ḥanafī and Shāfiʿī jurists and most Muʿtazilites infer from the verse that beneficial things are permissible before revealed law; al-Rāzī and al-Bayḍāwī choose this position.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p214#3/r8.anchor: واستدل كثير من أهل السنة الحنفية والشافعية بالآية على إباحة الأشياء النافعة قبل ورود الشرع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r1.claim: Against the benefit-based inference, some note that the lām can have other uses, as in “if you do evil, it is against you”; the reply treats its association as beneficial ownership or particularization.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r1.anchor: واعترض بأن اللام تجيء لغير النفع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r2.claim: Restricting the benefit to religious inference is contrary to the apparent sense; since every accountable person can infer from creation, the wording should extend to other benefits too.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r2.anchor: وبأن المراد النفع بالإستدلال وأجيب بأن التخصيص خلاف الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r3.claim: Other positions hold that things default to prohibition before a prohibition is stated, or suspend judgment because the evidence appears conflicting.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r3.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أن الأصل في الأشياء قبل الحظر وقال قوم بالوقف لتعارض الأدلة عندهم

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r4.claim: Libertarians argue that because everything is created for all, no one may have exclusive possession; the verse instead allows collective benefit alongside warranted individual assignments, determined by separate evidence.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r4.anchor: واستدلت الإباحية بالآية على مدعاهم قائلين إنها تدل على أن ما في الأرض جميعا خلق للكل فلا يكون لأحد اختصاص بشيء أصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r5.claim: ما can include everything on earth, even the earth itself, if “earth” means the lower region; alternatively the encompassing Throne or a conceptual direction explains how it can be included.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r5.anchor: تعم جميع ما في الأرض لأنفسها إذ لا يكون الشيء ظرفا لنفسه إلا أن يراد بها جهة السفل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r6.claim: One explanation includes every part of the earth because parts are necessary to it and their distinction from the whole is conceptual; the author rejects adding “and the earth” as an explicit omitted object.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r6.anchor: نعم قيل تعم كل جزء من أجزاء الأرض فإنه من جملة ضروراتها ما فيها ضرورة وجود الجزء في الكل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r7.claim: جميعا is an emphatic circumstantial accusative from ما, not evidence that all things were created simultaneously; taking it from لكم or الأرض conflicts with the context and emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r7.anchor: ولا دلالة لهما كما ذكره البعض على الإجتماع الزماني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r8.speaker: الربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains استوى إلى السماء as rising and ascending toward it without specifying how, likening it, or delimiting it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r8.anchor: أي علا إليها وارتفع من غير تكييف ولا تمثيل ولا تحديد قاله الربيع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r9.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains it as turning toward the heaven with an unimpeded, straight intention, from the expression for aiming like a released arrow.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r9.anchor: أو قصد إليها بإرادته قصدا سويا بلا صارف يلويه ولا عاطف يثنيه من قولهم استوى إليه كالسهم المرسل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r10.claim: A further interpretation takes استوى as prevailed over and possessed, supported by a line describing conquerors who rose over their foes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215/r10.anchor: وقيل استولى وملك كما في قوله فلما علونا واستوينا عليهم تركناهم صرعى لنسر وكاسر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r1.claim: Taking istawā as domination conflicts with the apparent sense by making ilā mean ʿalā and requiring a strained account of domination over creating heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r1.anchor: وهو خلاف الظاهر لاقتضائه كون ﴿ إلى ﴾ بمعنى على وأيضا الإستيلاد مؤخر عن وجود المستولى عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r2.claim: Here heaven may mean the celestial bodies or the direction above.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r2.anchor: والمراد بالسماء الإجرام العلوية أو جهة العلو

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r3.claim: One explanation takes thumma as temporal succession.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r3.anchor: ثم قيل للتراخي في الوقت وقيل لتفاوت ما بين الخلقين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r4.claim: Another explanation takes thumma to mark the difference in rank and the superior merit of heaven's creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r4.anchor: وقيل لتفاوت ما بين الخلقين وفضل خلق السماء على خلق الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r5.speaker: بعض
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r5.claim: Some hold that the heavens were created before the earth, citing the account of heaven's construction and the earth's subsequent spreading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r5.anchor: فذهب بعض إلى تقدم خلق السموات لقوله تعالى ﴿ أم السماء بناها رفع سمكها فسواها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r6.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r6.claim: Others hold that the earth was created first, citing the passage that places earth's creation and provisions before God's turning to heaven.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r6.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى تقدم خلق الأرض لقوله تعالى ( أئنكم لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين )

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r7.claim: A harmonization reads earth's later spreading as the completion, arrangement, and preparation of its contents for benefit, not the later creation of the earth itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r7.anchor: إن ( أخرج منها ماءها ) بدل أو عطف بيان ( لدحاها ) أي بسطها مبين للمراد منه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḥākim and al-Bayhaqī report from Ibn ʿAbbās, with a sound chain, a reconciliation of the two creation passages that points to this distinction between earth and its spreading.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r8.anchor: وما رواه الحاكم والبيهقي بسند صحيح عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما في التوفيق بين الآيتين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r9.claim: A report authenticated by Ibn Jarīr and others says Jews asked the Prophet about creation: earth on Sunday and Monday, mountains and benefits Tuesday, other provisions Wednesday, heaven Thursday, and celestial bodies and angels Friday.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r9.anchor: ولا يعارضه ما رواه إبن جرير وغيره وصححوه عنه أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.claim: The report's towns and inhabited places can refer to their matter and origins, since fully formed towns could not precede the earth's completion.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r10.anchor: لجواز أن يحمل على أنه خلق مادة ذلك وأصوله إذ لا يتصور المدائن والعمران والخراب قبل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that a vast earth cannot be created without being spread, so delayed spreading would entail delayed creation of the earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p215#2/r11.anchor: وإستشكال الإمام الرازي تأخر التدحية عن خلق السماء بأن الأرض جسم عظيم فأمتنع إنفكاك خلقها عن التدحية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r1.claim: Al-Rāzī's objection overlooks that advocates of delayed spreading say the earth began small, like a pestle head, and was spread later.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r1.anchor: على الغفلة لأن من يقول بتأخر دحوها عن خلقها لا يقول بعظمها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r2.claim: The claim that earthly things require a spread earth is answered by taking the early creation to mean their materials and origins, not their present forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r2.anchor: إن خلق الأشياء في الأرض لا يمكن إلا إذا كانت مدحوة لا يخفى دفعه بناء على أن المراد بذلك خلق المواد والأصول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r3.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r3.claim: Al-Wāḥidī transmits from Muqātil that the heavens came first, a view chosen by later investigators; they agree that all visible earthly contents came after the seven heavens.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r3.anchor: نقل الإمام الواحدي عن مقاتل الأول وأختاره المحققون ولم يختلفوا في أن جميع ما في الأرض مما ترى مؤخر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r4.claim: To reconcile the chronology, khalq can mean determination, or creation can be intended rather than actualized; the verse then says God intended the earth's contents for human benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r4.anchor: يجعل الخلق في الآية الكريمة بمعنى التقدير لا الإيجاد أو بمعناه ويقدر الإرادة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r5.claim: On the intention reading, the earth's later spreading describes actual formation after the heavens, while the prior event was the determination or will to create it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r5.anchor: فإن المتقدم على خلق السماء إنما هو تقدير الأرض وجميع ما فيها أو إرادة إيجادها والمتأخر عن خلق السماء إيجاد الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r6.claim: Likewise, “created the earth in two days” and “placed mountains therein” can mean that God intended their creation and placement.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r6.anchor: فعلى تقدير الإرادة والمعنى أراد خلق الأرض وكذا ( وجعل فيها رواسي ) ينبغي أن يكون بمعنى أراد أن يجعل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r7.claim: The command for heaven and earth to come suggests that the earth was not yet existent; both obeyed the creative command, after which the heavens and earth's contents were brought into being.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r7.anchor: فإن الظاهر أن المراد أئتيا في الوجود ولو كانت الأرض موجودة سايقة لما صح هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r8.claim: The earth-first order in al-Baqara and Fuṣṣilat suits their emphasis on beneficence to people; al-Nāziʿāt leads with heaven because its context displays power.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r8.anchor: لأن المقام في الأولين مقام الامتنان فمقتضاه تقديم ما هو نعمة نظرا إلى المخاطبين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r9.speaker: بعض القوم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r9.claim: Some statements of the sages imply that the encompassing heaven preceded earth; earth itself came next, then the seven heavens, earthly minerals and plants, animals, and humans.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r9.anchor: أن المحدد ويقال له سماء أيضا مخلوق قبل الأرض وما فيها وأن الأرض نفسها خلقت بعد ثم بعد خلقها خلقت السموات السبع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r10.claim: Under that cosmology, “created for you what is on earth” means decreed, intended, or initially materialized it; Fuṣṣilat's creation of earth can retain its ordinary sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p216/r10.anchor: قدره أو أراد إيجاده أو أوجد مواده

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r1.claim: The command to heaven and earth can mean that each manifests its latent effects and varied creatures, that heaven comes into being and earth is spread, or that they jointly generate what is intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r1.anchor: لجواز حمله على معنى ائتيا بما خلقت فيكما من التأثير والتأثر وإبراز ما أودعتكما من الأوضاع المختلفة والكائنات المتنوعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r2.claim: The disagreement over the sequence of creation is difficult and has remained difficult since the time of the Companions; the author hopes to revisit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r2.anchor: ولا زال الناس يستصعبونه من عهد الصحابة رضي الله تعالى عنهم الآن ولنا فيه إن شاء الله تعالى عودة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r3.claim: The pronoun refers to heaven if heaven means celestial bodies; it may also refer back as a plural or construed plural, otherwise it is an ambiguous pronoun explained by what follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r3.anchor: الضمير للسماء إن فسرت بالأجرام وجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r4.claim: Leaving the referent initially ambiguous magnifies it, builds anticipation, and fixes it in the listener's mind.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r4.anchor: وفيه من التفخيم والتشويق والتمكين في النفس ما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r5.claim: Seven has five proposed parses: apposition to the ambiguous referent or heaven, object after “made,” prospective circumstantial accusative, specification, or a second object if the verb means “made into.”
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r5.anchor: البدل من المبهم أو العائد إلى السماء أو مفعول به اي سوى منهن

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r6.claim: Apposition is the strongest parse because the numeral is not derived; the circumstantial reading comes next, as al-Baḥr notes.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r6.anchor: لعدم الإشتقاق وبعدها الحالية كما في البحر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r7.claim: God perfected, balanced, and created the heavens from the outset free of crookedness and fissures; the wording does not imply a later repair.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r7.anchor: أتمهن وقومهن وخلقهن ابتداء مصونات عن العوج والفطور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r8.claim: The correspondence between taswiya and istiwā has an evident rhetorical grace.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r8.anchor: وفي مقارنة التسوية والإستواء حسن لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r9.claim: Astronomers remain uncertain whether the spheres number nine, eight, seven, or can be reduced to one; their observations do not settle the count.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r9.anchor: هم شاكون إلى الآن في النقصان والزيادة فإن ما وجدوه من الحركات يمكن ضبطها بثمانية وسبعة بل بواحد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r10.speaker: بعض محققيهم
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r10.claim: Some of their investigators say it has not been established whether the sphere of fixed stars is one sphere or nested spheres.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r10.anchor: لم يتبين لي إلى الآن أن كرة الثوابت كرة واحدة أو كرات منطوية بعضها على بعض

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r11.speaker: الإمام الرازي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r11.claim: Al-Rāzī discusses the astronomical question at length and well; even a commonly accepted count of nine would not make this verse exclude additional spheres.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r11.anchor: وأطال الإمام الرازي الكلام في ذلك وأجاد على أنه إن صح ما شاع فليس في الآية ما يدل على نفي الزوائد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r12.speaker: الإمام البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r12.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī's commentary suggests that naming seven does not necessarily deny more, contrary to his al-Minhāj position aligned with al-Shāfiʿī and transmitted by al-Ghazālī.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r12.anchor: وكلام البيضاوي في تفسيره يشير إليه خلافا لما في منهاجه الموافق لما عليه الإمام الشافعي ونقله عنه الغزالي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r13.speaker: الساليكوتي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r13.claim: Al-Sālikūtī says the correct view is that specifying a number does not prove there are no additional ones; if the Throne and Footstool are spheres, nothing further remains to discuss.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r13.anchor: وذكر الساليكوتي أن الحق أن تخصيص العدد بالذكر لا يدل على نفي الزائد والخلاف في ذلك مشهور

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r14.claim: The closing declaration reinforces the preceding account of the extraordinary creation of the heavens, earth, and their contents, as in the description of creation without discrepancy.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r14.anchor: تذييل مقرر لما قبله من خلق السموات والأرض وما فيها على هذا النمط العجيب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r15.claim: ʿAlīm is more emphatic than ʿālim because divine knowledge encompasses universals and particulars, existent and nonexistent things, and finite and infinite realities, not because God's knowledge is multiple.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r15.anchor: من المبالغة ما ليس في عالم وليس ذلك راجعا إلى نفس الصفة لأن علمه تعالى واحد لا تكثر فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r16.claim: The word “thing” remains universal here and is not restricted, despite the contrary view the author condemns.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r16.anchor: والشيء هنا عام باق على عمومه لا تخصيص فيه بوجه خلافا لمن ضل عن سواء السبيل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r17.claim: The prepositional phrase modifies ʿalīm; emphatic participles can govern like afʿal tafḍīl, taking bi with knowledge or ignorance verbs, li otherwise, or their verb's usual preposition.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p217/r17.anchor: مع أنه من علم وهو متعد بنفسه والتقوية تكون باللام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r6.claim: God created all that is on earth so people may reflect and infer; another reported purpose is that they may benefit from it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r6.anchor: لكي تعتبروا وتستدلوا وقيل لكي تنتفعوا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر مفسري السلف
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and most early exegetes explain istawa as rising or ascending to heaven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر مفسري السلف: أي ارتفع إلى السماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r8.speaker: ابن كيسان والفراء وجماعة من النحويين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r8.claim: Ibn Kaysan, al-Farra, and a group of grammarians understand the phrase as turning to create heaven.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن كيسان والفراء وجماعة من النحويين: أي أقبل على خلق السماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r9.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r9.claim: Another explanation is that God intended to create heaven after creating earth first.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: قصد لأنه خلق الأرض أولا ثم عمد إلى خلق السماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r10.claim: God made the seven heavens even, without fissures or cracks.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r10.anchor: خلقهن مستويات لا فطور فيها ولا صدع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو والكسائي وقالون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r11.claim: Abu Ja'far, Abu Amr, al-Kisa'i, and Qalun give a sukun to the h in huwa and hiya after waw, fa, or lam; al-Kisa'i and Qalun also do so after thumma, and Qalun in the cited phrase.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p77#2/r11.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأبو عمرو والكسائي وقالون وهو وهي بسكون الهاء إذا كان قبل الهاء واو أو فاء أو لام

BURSEVI:v1p71/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71/r3.claim: This states another divine blessing: earthly things were apportioned for people's benefit in worldly and religious life, though not all were created at that moment.
BURSEVI:v1p71/r3.anchor: قدر خلقها لأجلكم ولانتفاعكم بها في دنياكم ودينكم

BURSEVI:v1p71/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71/r4.claim: The phrase means all the things contained in the earth.
BURSEVI:v1p71/r4.anchor: {ما في الأرض} أي : الذي فيها من الأشياء

BURSEVI:v1p71/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71/r5.claim: Jamīʿan is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of the second relative pronoun.

BURSEVI:v1p71/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r6.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v1p71/r6.claim: Al-Kawāshī says the verse can support the presumption that things are permissible by default.
BURSEVI:v1p71/r6.anchor: وقد يستدل بهذا على أن الأصل في الأشياء الإباحة كما في "الكواشي"

BURSEVI:v1p71/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r7.speaker: أهل الإباحة من المتصوفة الجهلة
BURSEVI:v1p71/r7.claim: Al-Taysīr reports ignorant libertine Sufis reading the phrase as unrestricted permission and claiming that realized love abolishes duties and prohibitions.
BURSEVI:v1p71/r7.anchor: أهل الإباحة من المتصوفة الجهلة حملوا اللام في لكم في قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p71/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71/r8.claim: Bursevī rejects unrestricted permission as explicit unbelief: revelation clearly preserves commands, prohibitions, permissions, promises, and warnings.
BURSEVI:v1p71/r8.anchor: وهذا منهم كفر صريح وقد نهى الله تعالى وأمر وأباح وحظر ووعد وأوعد

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r1.claim: Istawā ilā means that God directed His will toward creating the heaven without distraction or diversion to another act.
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r1.anchor: قصد إليها أي : إلى خلقها بإرادته ومشيئته قصدا سويا

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r2.claim: There is no contradiction with the statement that earth was spread afterward, because dahw means spreading it out.
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r2.anchor: ولا تناقض بين هذا وبين قوله

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that earth began at Jerusalem as a fist-sized stone under smoke; God raised the smoke into heavens and later spread the earth from the stone.
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن خلق الله الأرض في موضع بيت المقدس كهيئة الفهر أي : الحجر ملء الكف

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes a primordial jewel that melted into smoke and foam; the foam became earth and the smoke heaven.
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r5.claim: A further cosmological account says heaven came from smoke, rose by wind, dispersed by a gesture, stood without pillars, and was shattered by a breath.
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r5.anchor: قالوا فالسماء من دخان خلقت وبريح ارتفعت وبإشارة تفرقت

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r6.claim: Sawwāhunna means He perfected, straightened, and created the heavens complete, without crookedness or fissures.
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r6.anchor: أي : أتمهن وقومهن وخلقهن ابتداء مصونات عن العوج والفطور

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r7.claim: The pronoun in sawwāhunna is initially ambiguous, then explained by seven heavens; the phrase is a specification in the accusative.
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r7.anchor: والضمير فيه مبهم فسر بقوله تعالى : {سبع سماوات} فهو نصب على أنه تمييز

BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r8.speaker: سلمان
BURSEVI:v1p71#2/r8.claim: Salmān gives names and materials for the seven heavens: green emerald, white silver, red ruby, white pearl, red gold, yellow ruby, and gleaming light.

BURSEVI:v1p72/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72/r1.claim: God's knowledge explains the universe's excellent, beneficial order; perfected acts and wise specification imply a knowing, wise, merciful creator.
BURSEVI:v1p72/r1.anchor: فيه تعليل كأنه قال ولكونه عالما بكنه الأشياء كلها خلق ما خلق

BURSEVI:v1p72/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72/r2.claim: The verse answers doubts about resurrection: God can gather every body's scattered parts again without omission or adding foreign matter.
BURSEVI:v1p72/r2.anchor: وإزاحة لما يختلج في صدورهم من أن الأبدان بعدما تفتتت وتكسرت وتبددت أجزاؤها

BURSEVI:v1p72/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72/r3.claim: The seven heavens signify spiritual levels: earthly malakūt and psychic powers, the self, heart, intellect, secret, spirit, and hidden spiritual secret.
BURSEVI:v1p72/r3.anchor: وفي هذه الآية إشارة إلى مراتب الروحانيات

BURSEVI:v1p72/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r4.speaker: علي
BURSEVI:v1p72/r4.claim: ʿAlī says he knows heaven's paths better than earth's; Bursevī explains these paths as spiritual states and stations such as asceticism, piety, trust, and contentment.
BURSEVI:v1p72/r4.anchor: وإلى هذا أشار أمير المؤمنين علي رضي الله عنه بقوله : سلوني عن طرق السماء

BURSEVI:v1p72/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r5.speaker: الشيخ الشهير بافتادة أفندي
BURSEVI:v1p72/r5.claim: Aftāda Efendi counts twelve stations and says Jalwatīs traverse twelve gates through divine oneness, while Khalwatīs traverse them through the Names; he divides the gardens between their paths.
BURSEVI:v1p72/r5.anchor: وكان الشيخ الشهير بافتادة أفندي قدس سره يقول للتوحيد : اثنا عشر بابا

BURSEVI:v1p72/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p72/r6.claim: Bursevī relates the seven heavens to seven gardens attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās: four for the Jalwatīs of certainty and three for the Khalwatīs of the barzakh, acts, attributes, and essence.
BURSEVI:v1p72/r6.anchor: وهم يقولون جنة الأفعال وجنة الصفات وجنة الذات

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r6.claim: The inward reading says God created all things for humans, yet created humans for Himself; one should belong to Him rather than be occupied with possessions.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r6.anchor: أي : ما خلقكم لشيء وخلق كل شيء لكم بل خلقكم لنفسه كما قال تعالى : {واصطنعتك لنفسي}

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r7.claim: The cited saying promises that whoever belongs to God will have God; this unique human readiness conceals a profound secret of lordship.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r7.anchor: فبقدر ما تكون لي أكون لك كما قال عليه السلام :

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r8.claim: The heavens and earth exist subordinately to humanity's creation.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r8.anchor: فيه إشارة إلى أن وجود السموات والأرض كان تبعا لوجود الإنسان

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r9.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r9.claim: God knows each created thing and its purpose; every atom praises Him, testifies to His oneness, and affirms that creation is not in vain.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r9.anchor: أي : عالم بخلق كل شيء خلقه ولأي شيء خلقه فكل ذرة

BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r10.speaker: الجامي
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r10.claim: Al-Jāmī's couplet presents the two worlds as the arena of God's existence and a witness to His oneness.
BURSEVI:v1p72#2/r10.anchor: دوجهان جلوكاه وجدت تو شهد الله كواه وحدت تو

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r1.claim: This is a further favor following the gift of life: God created what sustains people and completes their livelihood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r1.anchor: بيان نعمة أخرى مرتبة على الأولى

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r2.claim: For your sake means worldly benefit to bodies, directly or through means, and religious benefit through reflection and recognition of afterlife joys and pains; this is not a purpose that perfects God, but an outcome of His act.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r2.anchor: في مصالح أبدانكم بوسط أو بغير وسط

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r3.claim: The wording indicates that useful things are permitted, without implying that every thing belongs to every individual; the common grant can be apportioned for incidental reasons.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r4.claim: ما encompasses everything on earth only if الأرض means the lower realm, just as السماء can mean the upper realm.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r4.anchor: إلا إذا أريد بها جهة السفل كما يراد بالسماء جهة العلو

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29/r5.claim: جميعا is a circumstantial accusative qualifying the second relative pronoun.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.claim: He prefers ‘turned toward the heaven by His will,’ comparing it to an arrow aimed straight; this fits the word’s root, its preposition, and the following creation. He rejects bodily ‘became even’ as a property of bodies; ‘mastered’ is another reported sense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.anchor: من قولهم استوى إليه كالسهم المرسل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r2.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r2.claim: An alternative gloss takes استوى as ‘mastered and ruled,’ supported by the poetic line about Bishr ruling Iraq without sword or bloodshed.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.claim: The heaven means either the celestial bodies or the upper regions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالسماء هذه الأجرام العلوية، أو جهات العلو

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.claim: ثم may mark the difference and superiority of the heavens over the earth, rather than temporal sequence, which would conflict with the apparent meaning of 79:30; an alternative reading there supplies a later act of spreading the earth, but is less apparent.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.anchor: لعله لتفاوت ما بين الخلقين وفضل خلق السماء على خلق الأرض

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.claim: God formed the heavens evenly, protected from crookedness and fissures.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.anchor: عدلهن وخلقهن مصونة من العوج والفطور

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.claim: The pronoun هن refers to heaven as celestial bodies, which is plural, or to heaven as a plural notion; otherwise it is an ambiguous pronoun explained by what follows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.anchor: ضمير السماء إن فسرت بالأجرام لأنه جمع

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r3.claim: سبع سموات is either an appositive or an explanatory gloss.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.claim: The astronomers’ nine spheres are uncertain; even if established, the verse does not exclude additional spheres, and including the Throne and Footstool removes the disagreement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.anchor: فيما ذكروه شكوك، وإن صح فليس في الآية نفي الزائد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r5.claim: God’s complete knowledge explains the excellent, beneficial order of creation and is demonstrated by its precise, wise, merciful design.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.claim: This knowledge removes doubt about gathering bodily parts after they have dispersed and mixed with similar matter; 36:79 likewise invokes God’s knowledge of every creation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.anchor: وإزاحة لما يختلج في صدورهم من أن الأبدان بعدما تبددت

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.claim: The resurrection proof has three premises: body matter can be assembled and revived, shown by its recurring separation, joining, death, and life in 2:28; God knows its parts and locations; and He can assemble and revive them, as shown by His ability to originate them and create greater things.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.anchor: أما الأولى فهي: أن مواد الأبدان قابلة للجمع والحياة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
