BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.claim: The flawless, beneficial order of creation demonstrates the knowledge and complete wisdom needed for the other premises of resurrection.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.anchor: وأنه تعالى خلق ما خلق خلقا مستويا محكما من غير تفاوت واختلال مراع فيه مصالحهم وسد حاجاتهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.claim: Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and al-Kisāʾī pronounce the هاء in forms such as فهو and وهو with sukūn, by analogy with عضد.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.anchor: وقد سكن نافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي: الهاء من نحو فهو وهو

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r3.claim: Biqai says the verse unpacks the earlier summary of human beginnings, middle, and end: creation is an act of favor that calls people to God through proof of power and kindness that elicits love.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r3.anchor: ليكون داعيا إلى توحيده من وجهين : كونه دالا على عظمة مؤثرة وكمال قدرته ,

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r4.claim: Al-Harali reads “He” as pointing to the transcendent unseen God who sustains everything; the divine essence remains hidden while the names disclose Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r4.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهي كلمة مدلولها العلي غيب الإلهية القائم بكل شيء الذي لا يظهر لشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r5.claim: The address warns persistent disbelievers after promising their return, using a threat that may draw them back willingly or by force.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r5.anchor: قال : لما انتهى الخطاب بذكر إرجاعهم إلى الله وكان هذا خطابا خاصا مع المتمادي على كفره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r6.claim: The warning is like a slack rope that may draw a person back through divine kindness or pull him forcibly at the end of his turning away.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r6.anchor: قال : لما انتهى الخطاب بذكر إرجاعهم إلى الله وكان هذا خطابا خاصا مع المتمادي على كفره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r7.claim: Al-Harali says the ending of the call echoes its opening, though this verse sharply separates its two ends by moving from the unseen divine name to tangible earthly creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r7.anchor: وانتظم به ختم آية الدعوة بنحو من ابتدائها , إلا أن هذه على نهاية الاقتطاع بين طرفيها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r8.claim: God created what is on earth for people as a kindness to them in both their religious and worldly lives.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r8.anchor: { الذي خلق لكم } دينا ودنيا لطفا بكم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r9.claim: Al-Harali says “all” signals that human needs depend on the whole of earthly creation; losing one element causes others to falter.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r9.anchor: قال الحرالي : وقوله : { جميعا } إعلان بأن حاجة الإنسان لا تقوم بشيء دون شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r10.claim: The verse establishes that created things are presumptively permissible; nothing is prohibited without evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r10.anchor: والآية دليل على أن الأصل في الأشياء الإباحة , فلا يمنع شيء إلا بدليل .

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r11.claim: The elevated heaven, firm construction, ordered beauty, and many benefits warrant the connective “then,” which magnifies its rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r11.anchor: ولما كانت السماء أشرف من جهة العلو الذي لا يرام , والجوهر البالغ في الأحكام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r12.claim: God turned His will toward arranging the heaven, whose height, beauty, purity, and abundant benefits are emphasized.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r12.anchor: ثم علق إرادته ومشيئته بتسويتها من غير أدنى عدول ونظر إلى غيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r13.claim: Al-Harali notes that heaven is where people fear harmful events will descend, so the verse reassures them that God governs the very realm they fear.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r13.anchor: قال الحرالي : أعلى الخطاب بذكر الاستواء إلى السماء الذي هو موضع التخوف لهم لنزول المخوفات منه عليهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r14.claim: The fitting sense of divine istiwāʾ concerns rank and unseen realities, not a restriction to bodily locations and sensory appearances.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r14.anchor: مجرى لفظ الاستواء في الرتبة والمكانة أحق بمعناه من موقعه في المكان والشهادة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r15.claim: The singular “heaven” can indicate the elevated direction or the heavenly kind; the following plural pronoun signals the seven individual heavens.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r15.anchor: الإفراد الصالح لجهة العلو تنبيها على الشرف , وللجنس الصالح للكثرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r16.claim: The earth was created and prepared before the heaven, then spread out afterward; “then” can mark exaltation rather than sequence, and earth is mentioned first because it is closer to human experience.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r16.anchor: فكان خلق الأرض وتهيئتها لما يراد منها قبل خلق السماء , ودحوها بعد خلق السماء ؛ على أن ثم للتعظيم لا للترتيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r17.claim: The verse puts earth first because its close connection to human beings makes it a more immediate sign.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r17.anchor: وتقديم الأرض هنا لأنها أدل لشدة الملابسة والمباشرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r18.claim: Making the heavens even means giving each constituent its due so that the whole reaches its perfected form.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p81/r18.anchor: التسوية إعطاء أجزاء الشيء حظه لكمال صورة ذلك الشيء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r1.claim: Biqai completes the implied benefit: everything in the heavens was also created for human use.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r1.anchor: وخلق جميع ما فيها لكم , فالآية من الاحتباك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r2.claim: The verse uses the rare figure of ḥatbāk: the seven earthly levels are omitted because the seven heavens indicate them, and heavenly benefits are omitted because earthly benefits already indicate them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r2.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك ؛ حذف أولا كون الأراضي سبعا لدلالة الثاني عليه , وثانيا كون ما في السماء لنا لدلالة الأول عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r3.claim: The ordered creation proves the maker’s power; since its arrangement rests on knowledge, the verse ends by naming knowledge and thereby affirms His power over all things.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r3.anchor: ولما كان الخلق على هذه الكيفية دالا بالبديهة على أتم قدرة لصانعه وكان العلم بأن مبنى ذلك على العلم محتاجا إلى تأمل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r4.claim: After the visible cycles of life and death point to resurrection, the ordered cosmos and its knowledge-bearing close prepare the account of humanity’s creation and its gift of knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p83/r4.anchor: ولما ذكر الحياة والموت المشاهدين تنبيها على القدرة

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r6.claim: Qatada says God subjected everything on earth for Adam's honor and blessing, as provision, sustenance, and benefit for a limited term.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا} قال: سخر لكم ما في الأرض جميعا كرامة من الله ونعمة لابن آدم

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r7.claim: Mujahid says earth was made useful to people, preceded heaven, and its smoke became heaven; God made seven heavens above and seven earths below.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا} قال: سخر لكم ما في الأرض جميعا

DURR-FULL:v1p105/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r8.claim: A report via al-Suddi from Abu Malik, Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas, Murra al-Hamdani, Ibn Masud, and Companions says God's Throne was on water; smoke rose from it, then the water dried and was split into seven earths.
DURR-FULL:v1p105/r8.anchor: من طريق السدي عن أبي مالك وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس وعن مرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وعن ناس من أصحاب رسول الله

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r1.claim: Earth rests on a fish, beneath which are water, a slab, an angel, a rock, and wind; the rock is Luqman's, while the fish's movement shook earth until mountains anchored it. The fish is linked to 68:1.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r1.anchor: فخلق الأرض على حوت وهو الذي ذكره في قوله (ن والقلم) والحوت في الماء والماء على ظهر صفاة والصفاة على ظهر ملك

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r2.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r2.claim: The report says mountains steadied earth and cites the verse about mountains being set so earth would not shake beneath people.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r2.anchor: فتزلزلت الأرض فأرسى عليها الجبال فالجبال تفخر على الأرض فذلك قوله (وجعل لها رواسي أن تميد بكم)

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r3.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r3.claim: Mountains, inhabitants' provisions, trees, and other needs were created on Tuesday and Wednesday; the report links this to 41:9–10.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r3.anchor: وخلق الجبال فيها وأقوات أهلها وشجرها وما ينبغي لها في يومين: في الثلاثاء والأربعاء

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r4.claim: Water's smoke became one heaven, then was divided into seven over Thursday and Friday; Friday was named for the joining of heaven and earth's creation, linking to 41:11.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r4.anchor: ثم جعلها سماء واحدة ثم فتقها فجعلها سبع سموات في يومين: في الخميس والجمعة وإنما سمي يوم الجمعة لأنه جمع فيه خلق السموات والأرض

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r5.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r5.claim: The report says God created inhabitants in every heaven, including angels and other beings such as seas and hail mountains, some unknown to people.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r5.anchor: قال: خلق في كل سماء خلقها من الملائكة والخلق الذي فيها من البحار وجبال البرد ومما لا يعلم

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r6.claim: After completing creation, God adorned the sky with stars as decoration and protection from devils, then settled upon the Throne.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r6.anchor: ثم زين السماء بالكواكب فجعلها زينة وحفظا من الشياطين فلما فرغ من خلق ما أحب استوى على العرش

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says God made seven heavens by heating water so its vapor rose into the air and formed them.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ثم استوى إلى السماء} يعني خلق سبع سموات قال: أجرى النار على الماء فبخر البحر فصعد في الهواء فجعل السموات منها

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r8.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r8.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses “turned toward” the heaven as “rose.”
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r8.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {ثم استوى إلى السماء} قال: ارتفع

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r9.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r9.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains “fashioned them” as making their creation even and well formed.

DURR-FULL:v1p106/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r10.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr says the Throne preceded earth and sky; wind stirred water and produced smoke for heavens, clay for earth, and foam for mountains.
DURR-FULL:v1p106/r10.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو قال: لما أراد الله أن يخلق الأشياء إذا كان عرشه على الماء وإذ لا أرض ولا سماء خلق الريح فسلطها على الماء

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r1.speaker: سلمان الفارسي
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r1.claim: Salman al-Farisi gives each heaven's material and name: green emerald Raqi'a, white silver Azqalon, red ruby Qaydum, white pearl Ma'una, red gold Riq'a, yellow ruby Daqna, and light Ariba.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r1.anchor: عن سلمان الفارسي قال: السماء الدنيا من زمردة خضراء واسمها رقيعاء والثانية من فضة بيضاء واسمها أزقلون والثالثة من ياقوتة حمراء

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r2.claim: Ali says the lowest heaven is called Raqi and the seventh is called al-Surakh.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r2.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال: اسم السماء الدنيا رقيع واسم السابعة الصراخ

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the heaven containing the Throne the chief of the heavens and the earth people inhabit the chief of the earths.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: سيد السموات السماء التي فيها العرش وسيد الأرضين الأرض التي أنتم عليها

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r4.speaker: أبو الجلد
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r4.claim: In a letter to Abu al-Jald, Ibn Abbas asks what the heaven is made of; Abu al-Jald replies that it is a contained wave.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r4.anchor: عن الشعبي قال: كتب ابن عباس إلى أبي الجلد يسأله عن السماء من أي شيء هي فكتب إليه: إن السماء من موج مكفوف

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r5.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r5.claim: Hibba al-Awfi says he heard Ali swear that God created the heaven from smoke and water.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r5.anchor: عن حبة العوفي قال: سمعت عليا ذات يوم يحلف والذي خلق السماء من دخان وماء

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r6.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r6.claim: Ka'b says the heaven is whiter than milk.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r6.anchor: عن كعب قال: السماء أشد بياضا من اللبن

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r7.speaker: سفيان الثوري
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r7.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri reports that beneath the earths is a rock, and it is said the sky's green color comes from it.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r7.anchor: عن سفيان الثوري قال: تحت الأرضين صخرة بلغنا أن تلك الصخرة منها خضرة السماء

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas counsels contemplating creation rather than God's essence, saying seven thousand lights lie between the seventh heaven and God's Kursi and He is above that.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: تفكروا في كل شيء ولا تفكروا في ذات الله فإن بين السماء السابعة إلى كرسيه سبعة آلاف نور

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r9.claim: Qatada says the seven heavens are layered, with a journey of five hundred years between each pair.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {فسواهن سبع سماوات} قال: بعضهن فوق بعض بين كل سمائين مسيرة خمسمائة عام

DURR-FULL:v1p109/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r10.claim: Ibn Masud says the fairest verse in the Qur'an is one whose ending is a name of God.
DURR-FULL:v1p109/r10.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن أعدل آية في القرآن آخرها اسم من أسماء الله تعالى

IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r1.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says creation proceeded by days: soil Saturday, mountains Sunday, trees Monday, unpleasant things Tuesday, light Wednesday, animals Thursday, and Adam late Friday.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : اخذ رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بيدي فقال : خلق الله التربة يوم السبت

IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r2.claim: Mujahid says earth was created before heaven; smoke rose from the earth, as described in 41:11, and the heavens and earths are layered above and below one another.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا قال : خلق الله الأرض قبل السماء ، فلما خلق الأرض ثار منها دخان

IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r3.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says the throne rested over water; smoke became heaven, water became one earth then split into seven, and earth rested on a whale over a layered support before mountains stabilized it. Provisions were apportioned over four days.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p74/r3.anchor: فخلق الأرض على حوت ، والحوت هو النون الذي ذكر الله في القران

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r1.claim: Qatadah explains that God subjected everything on earth for humankind as a favor and blessing to Adam's children.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قول الله : هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا اي سخر لكم ما في الأرض جميعا كرامة من الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya glosses God's istiwa toward heaven as rising; Hasan and al-Rabi ibn Anas are reported to agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r2.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : ثم استوى إلى السماء يقول : ارتفع

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r3.claim: Qatadah says the seven heavens lie one above another, with a journey of five hundred years between each pair.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : فسواهن سبع سموات قال بعضهن فوق بعض ، بين كل سمائين مسيرة خمسمائة عام

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains “made them even” as perfecting their creation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r4.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله : فسواهن يقول : سوى خلقهن

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r5.claim: Mujahid says the seven heavens are above one another and the seven earths below one another.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله : فسواهن سبع سموات بعضهن فوق بعض ، وسبع ارضين بعضهن تحت بعض

IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains God's knowledge here as knowledge of people's deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p75/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قول الله : وهو بكل شئ عليم يعني من اعمالكم عليم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r1.claim: The verse may be a second proof, escalating from human creation to the many earthly creatures; alternatively it is a favor statement embedding proof of God’s creative power, with لكم marking benefit to people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r1.anchor: دلائل ربوبية الله ووحدانيته ظاهرة في خلق الإنسان وفي خلق جميع ما في الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r2.claim: The uncoordinated sentence may signal close connection: earthly provisions complete the existence begun in 2:28; alternatively, omitting conjunction shows the first proof stands independently, though Ibn Ashur notes drawbacks to both analyses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r2.anchor: وفصل الجملة السابقة يجوز أن يكون لمراعاة كمال الاتصال بين الجملتين لأن هذه كالنتيجة للدليل الأول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r3.claim: Earth is the spherical world of land and sea inhabited by people and containing animals, plants, and minerals; the verse names what is within it because those visible kinds invite reflection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r3.anchor: والأرض اسم للعالم الكروي المشتمل على البر والبحر الذي يعمره الإنسان والحيوان والنبات والمعادن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r4.claim: Although the verse attaches creation to earth’s contents rather than to earth itself, it implies God created the container: the container cannot sensibly be later than its contents or precede them pointlessly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r4.anchor: فاستفادة أنه خلق الأرض مأخوذة بطريق الفحوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows “earth” to mean the lower region, parallel to “heaven” as the upper region; Ibn Ashur rejects this because earth literally names the globe and only figuratively a region.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p378/r5.anchor: فمن البعيد أن يجوز صاحب ( الكشاف ) أن يراد بالأرض الجهة السفلية كما يراد بالسماء الجهة العلوية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r1.claim: Earth is a visible thing, whereas sky names what is elevated and shades; the terms do not simply denote opposite directions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r1.anchor: السماء أطلقت على كل ما علا فأظل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r2.claim: The clause is a true exclusivity addressed to idolaters who knew God created but acted as though ignorant through shirk and neglect of worship and gratitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r2.anchor: صيغة قصر وهو قصر حقيقي سيق للمخاطبين من المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r3.claim: The reminder identifies God as creator of earth, its surface, and its interior, and says all this was created for human benefit across changing times and circumstances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r3.anchor: التذكير بأن الله هو خالق الأرض وما عليها وما في داخلها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r4.claim: The author compares the reminder with the claim that creator and noncreator are unlike and that idols cannot create even a fly; idolaters treated idols as intercessors, not creators.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r4.anchor: ما كانوا يثبتون لأصنامهم قدرة على الخلق وإنما جعلوها شفعاء ووسائط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r5.claim: The compact insertion of for you replaces a full explanation and displays divine power, favor, humanity's standing, and a reason to uproot disbelief.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r5.anchor: والمقصود من الكلام فيما أراه موافقا للبلاغة التذكير بأن الله هو خالق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r6.claim: The purposive lām raises whether divine acts have ends; Muslims agree acts follow divine will, choice, and knowledge and contain wisdoms and benefits, while dispute concerns calling these aims or final causes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r6.anchor: المسألة مختلف فيها بين المتكلمين اختلافا يشبه أن يكون لفظيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r7.speaker: جماعة المثبتين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r7.claim: A group affirms purposes in divine acts, adducing verses such as God's creation of jinn and humans to worship Him.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r8.speaker: أصحاب الأشعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p379/r8.claim: As Fakhr reports their view, Ashʿarī followers deny divine acts have purposes: an agent who acts for a purpose would benefit from it and need the cause.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r1.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء والمتكلمين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r1.claim: Al-Shāṭibī reports that most jurists and theologians regard God's rulings as grounded in interests and prevention of harms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r1.anchor: عن جمهور الفقهاء والمتكلمين أن أحكام الله تعالى معللة بالمصالح ودرء المفاسد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r2.speaker: ابن عرفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r2.claim: Ibn ʿArafa distinguishes the disputed grounding of God's acts from His rulings, which he says are grounded in interests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r2.anchor: هذا هو تعليل أفعال الله تعالى وفيه خلاف وأما أحكامه فمعللة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r3.speaker: الرازي والبيضاوي وصاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī, al-Bayḍāwī, al-Zamakhsharī, some Muʿtazilites and Shāfiʿī and Ḥanafī authorities infer that using things is originally permitted; the view is also attributed to al-Shāfiʿī.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r4.speaker: المالكية وجمهور الحنفية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r4.claim: Mālikīs and most Ḥanafīs, along with the Muʿtazilites in Ibn ʿArafa's report, hold that the original status of things is suspension and reject the verse as proof.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r4.anchor: وذهب المالكية وجمهور الحنفية والمعتزلة في نقل ابن عرفة إلى أن الأصل في الأشياء الوقف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r5.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī reads the verse as evidence of God's power, knowledge, ordering, and direction of created things, not as a rule of permissibility.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r6.claim: The verse is general and intended to alert people to the Creator's power; creation for humanity does not make every possible use lawful, and the verse addresses disbelievers rather than legislating for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r6.anchor: والحق أن الآية مجملة قصد منها التنبيه على قدرة الخالق بخلق ما في الأرض وأنه خلق لأجلنا إلا أن خلقه لأجلنا لا يستلزم إباحة استعماله في كل ما يقصد منه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r7.claim: The grant is for humanity collectively: the whole created domain belongs to people as a whole, not every item to every individual, as al-Bayḍāwī observes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r7.anchor: أن الآية ذكرت أن المجموع للمجموع لا كل واحد لكل واحد كما أشار إليه البيضاوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r8.speaker: بعض أهل الحديث وبعض المعتزلة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r8.claim: Some hadith scholars and some Muʿtazilites hold that things are originally forbidden; al-Qurṭubī notes that Muʿtazilites are reported to hold all three positions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r8.anchor: وذهب جماعة إلى أن أصل الأشياء الحظر ونقل عن بعض أهل الحديث وبعض المعتزلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r9.speaker: الإمام الرازي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī says the dispute matters especially for acts during the pre-prophetic interval and regards suspension as the sounder position, leaving things without a status that entails reward or punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p381/r9.anchor: وإنما تظهر ثمرة المسألة في حكم الأشياء أيام الفترة قبل النبوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r1.claim: The author says the pre-prophetic interval need not be framed this way: after revelation, where no text, analogy, or valid inference settles a case, harms are forbidden and benefits permitted, following al-Rāzī's al-Maḥṣūl.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r1.anchor: فإن وجد فعل لم يدل عليه دليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r2.claim: The discourse shifts from the familiar creation of earth to the greater creation of heaven, which people may overlook as evidence of God; the shift expands the reminder of divine power.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r2.anchor: انتقال من الاستدلال بخلق الأرض وما فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r3.claim: When clauses about one subject are joined by thumma, it can mark an imagined delay in rank: the following point is weightier and deserves renewed attention; the author illustrates this with al-Balad and a line by Ṭarafa.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p382/r3.anchor: للمهلة في الرتبة وهي مهلة تخييلية في الأصل تشير إلى أن المعطوف بثم أعرق في المعنى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r1.claim: Thumma usually marks rank when clauses report one subject, but real temporal succession when the subjects differ; 2:84–85 and the passing of two armies illustrate chronological order.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r1.anchor: أكثر ما يرد فيما إذا كانت الجمل إخبارا عن مخبر عنه واحد بخلاف ما إذا اختلف المخبر عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r2.claim: If heaven followed earth in creation, thumma marks both temporal and rank delay; if heaven came first, it marks rank alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r2.anchor: فأما هذه الآية فإنه إذا كانت السماوات متأخرا خلقها عن خلق الأرض فثم للتراخي الرتبي لا محالة مع التراخي الزمني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r3.speaker: الجمهور ومنهم مجاهد والحسن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r3.claim: Most early authorities, including Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan, with the view also attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās, place earth's creation before heaven, citing this verse and 41:9–11.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r3.anchor: قال الجمهور منهم مجاهد والحسن ونسب إلى ابن عباس إن خلق الأرض متقدم على خلق السماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r4.speaker: قتادة والسدي ومقاتل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r4.claim: Qatāda, al-Suddī, and Muqātil place heaven's creation before earth, citing the statement that earth was spread after heaven was built.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي ومقاتل إن خلق السماء متقدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r5.claim: The reconciliation is that earth was created first, heaven next, and earth's spreading came afterward; geological accounts describe cooling, crust formation, cracking, sinking, and uplift, though God could bring such change about quickly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r5.anchor: وقد أجيب بأن الأرض خلقت أولا ثم خلقت السماء ثم دحيت الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r6.claim: The author favors heaven before earth: after that in 79:30 states succession more clearly than thumma here, astronomy treats earth as detached from the sun, and Genesis appears to give the same order; Quranic summary avoids the dispute.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p383/r6.anchor: وأرجح القولين هو أن السماء خلقت قبل الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r1.claim: Sky may mean the atmosphere surrounding earth, which came after it, or the celestial bodies, which fit the seven heavens and may have preceded earth; Quranic passages may use either sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r1.anchor: والسماء إن أريد بها الجو المحيط بالكرة الأرضية فهو تابع لها متأخر عن خلقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r2.claim: Istiwāʾ basically means straightness; figuratively with ilā it means to direct oneself toward something resolutely and quickly, here likening God's decisive will to prepare for a great, exact work.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r2.anchor: ويطلق مجازا على القصد إلى الشيء بعزم وسرعة كأنه يسير إليه مستويا لا يلوي على شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r3.claim: The iftaʿala form is figurative and suggests that heaven and its inhabitants were created among the first things, as preparation for earth and ultimately humanity, the story's focus.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r3.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنه لما ابتدأ خلق المخلوقات خلق السماوات ومن فيها ليكون توطئة لخلق الأرض ثم خلق الإنسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r4.claim: Sawwāhun means that God created the heavens in ordered perfection without flaw or defect; istawā and sawwāhun form a modified paronomasia.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r4.anchor: أي خلقهن في استقامة ، واستقامة الخلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r5.claim: Samāʾ derives from elevation and can name one upper realm or the class of realms above earth; here it is generic because the verse says it was made seven heavens.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r5.anchor: والسماء مشتقة من السمو وهو العلو واسم السماء يطلق على الواحد وعلى الجنس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r6.claim: The pronoun hun returns to samāʾ understood generically as a plural; al-Zamakhsharī also allows samāʾ to mean the upper direction, which is possible but unnecessary according to al-Taftāzānī.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r6.anchor: باعتبار إرادة الجنس لأنه في معنى الجمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r7.claim: Although God alone knows the seven heavens' full nature, the author considers the likely scientific referent to be the great celestial bodies, the planets in the solar system with earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p384/r7.anchor: إلا أن الظاهر الذي دلت عليه القواعد العلمية أن المراد من السماوات الأجرام العلوية العظيمة وهي الكواكب السيارة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r1.claim: The declaration of universal knowledge follows from the signs of power: such creation can only issue from one who knows; it also rebukes the ugliness of disbelieving in the all-knowing God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r1.anchor: نتيجة لما ذكره من دلائل القدرة التي لا تصدر إلا من عليم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r2.speaker: جميع المليين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r2.claim: All religious communities affirm God's universal knowledge, while philosophers deny that He knows particulars; the author dismisses their claim as groundless.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r2.anchor: وقد قال بذلك جميع المليين كما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r3.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r3.claim: The majority read the hāʾ in huwa with ḍamma, the default vocalization.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور هاء ( وهو ) بالضم على الأصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r4.speaker: قالون وأبو عمرو والكسائي وأبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r4.claim: Qālūn, Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Jaʿfar read the hāʾ in huwa with sukūn to lighten it after a conjunction; this is common Arabic usage, supported by poetic meter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p386/r4.anchor: وقرأها قالون وأبو عمرو والكسائي وأبو جعفر بالسكون للتخفيف عند دخول حرف العطف عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r6.claim: Kh-l-q means to originate and bring into existence after nonexistence, though it can also describe a person creating something after its initial composition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r6.anchor: وخلق معناه اخترع وأوجد بعد العدم، وقد يقال في الإنسان خلق بعد إنشائه شيئا، ومنه قول الشاعر:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r7.claim: Zuhayr’s line and a second poet’s verse illustrate the human sense of creating after making something or creating what one says.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r7.anchor: ولأنت تفري ما خلقت وبعض ... القوم يخلق ثم لا يفري

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r8.claim: The phrase “for you” means for reflection, as nearby signs include life, death, creation, and the ordering of the heavens.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r8.anchor: ولكم: معناه للاعتبار، ويدل على ذلك ما قبله وما بعده من نصب العبر: الإحياء،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r9.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r9.claim: Some take “for you” to mean that things are permitted and placed in human ownership, supporting presumptive permissibility before revelation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: بل معنى لكم إباحة الأشياء وتمليكها، وهذا قول من يقول إن الأشياء قبل ورود السمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r10.speaker: القائلون بالحظر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r10.claim: Those who presume prohibition reject that reading; most make exceptions for necessities such as breathing and movement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r10.anchor: وخالفهم في هذا التأويل القائلون بالحظر، والقائلون بالوقف، وأكثر القائلين بالحظر استثنوا أشياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r11.speaker: القائلون بالوقف
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r11.claim: Suspension is preferable for a hypothetical case with no revealed evidence or textual attachment; it means exhausting the investigator’s effort on novel cases.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r11.anchor: ويترجح الوقف إذا قدرنا نازلة لا يوجد فيها سمع ولا تتعلق به. ومعنى الوقف أنه استنفاد جهد الناظر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r12.speaker: ابن الصائغ
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r12.claim: Ibn al-Sa'igh says, as quoted by Ibn Furak, that reason is never without scriptural evidence: a case has a relevant text or established prior state, dispensing with the three-way dispute.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r12.anchor: وحكى ابن فورك عن ابن الصائغ أنه قال: «لم يخل العقل قط من السمع ولا نازلة إلا وفيها سمع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r13.claim: Jamiʿan is an accusative circumstantial expression.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p114/r13.anchor: ويغني عن النظر في حظر وإباحة ووقف» ، وجميعا نصب على الحال.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r1.claim: God created everything on earth for human beings: some things are for use and others for reflection.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r1.anchor: أي لأجلكم فبعضه للانتفاع وبعضه للاعتبار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r2.claim: Here istawā ilā means that God turned to or intended the creation of heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r2.anchor: أي عمد إلى خلقها والسماء لفظها لفظ الواحد ومعناها معنى الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r3.claim: Al-samāʾ is singular in form but plural in meaning, as shown by the plural pronoun in fa-sawwāhunna.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r3.anchor: والسماء لفظها لفظ الواحد ومعناها معنى الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r4.claim: Mujāhid holds that earth was created before heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r4.anchor: وأيها أسبق في الخلق الأرض أم السماء فيه قولان أحدهما الأرض قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r5.claim: Muqātil holds that heaven was created before earth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says earth was created in two days, then the heavens in two, and its provisions were apportioned in two more.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r6.anchor: فقال ابن عباس بدأ بخلق الأرض في يومين ثم خلق السموات في يومين وقدر فيها أقواتها في يومين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r7.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r7.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujāhid say the creation of earth and everything in it took four consecutive days, followed by two days for heaven.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن و مجاهد جمع خلق الأرض وما فيها في أربعة أيام متوالية ثم خلق السماء في يومين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r8.claim: The intensive form ʿalīm emphasizes the perfection of God’s knowledge.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p58/r8.anchor: والعليم جاء على بناء فعيل للمبالغة في وصفه بكمال العلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.claim: After the evidence of human creation and experience, Ibn Kathir turns to the visible creation of the heavens and earth as another proof.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r1.anchor: لما ذكر تعالى دلالة من خلقهم وما يشاهدونه من أنفسهم، ذكر دليلا آخر مما يشاهدونه من خلق السماوات والأرض،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.claim: Here istiwaʾ means to intend or turn toward the heaven, since the verb is followed by ila.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r2.anchor: أي: قصد إلى السماء، والاستواء هاهنا تضمن (2) معنى القصد والإقبال؛ لأنه عدي بإلى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.claim: God made the heaven seven heavens; “heaven” is a generic noun, explaining the feminine plural pronoun in fasawahunna.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r3.anchor: والسماء هاهنا اسم جنس، فلهذا قال: {فسواهن} .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.claim: God's knowledge encompasses everything He created, as affirmed by the question in al-Mulk 14.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r4.anchor: أي: وعلمه محيط بجميع ما خلق (3) . كما قال: {ألا يعلم من خلق}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.claim: Fussilat 9–12 gives this creation account in detail and indicates that earth was created first, then the seven heavens; building begins with foundations and rises upward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r5.anchor: ففي هذا دلالة على أنه تعالى ابتدأ بخلق الأرض أولا ثم خلق السماوات سبعا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.claim: One explanation takes thumma in al-Naziʿat 30 to order the account's presentation rather than the events, supported by the cited poem about successive ancestors.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r6.anchor: كما قال الشاعر: قل لمن ساد ثم ساد أبوه … ثم قد ساد قبل ذلك جده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Talha, says the earth's spreading occurred after the heavens were created.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p213#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن الدحى كان بعد خلق السماوات، رواه ابن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r1.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r1.claim: Al-Suddi's report says the Throne was over water, smoke rose from water as the sky, and the water dried into one earth that was split into seven on Sunday and Monday.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r1.anchor: وقد قال السدي في تفسيره، عن أبي مالك -وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس-وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r2.claim: In the same report, earth rests on a fish identified with Nun; beneath it are water, a stone slab, an angel, another rock, and wind. The fish's movement shakes earth, so mountains stabilize it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r2.anchor: وقد قال السدي في تفسيره، عن أبي مالك -وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس-وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r3.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r3.claim: The report assigns Tuesday and Wednesday to mountains, provisions for earth's inhabitants, and vegetation; it glosses “for those who ask” as the explanation given to an inquirer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r3.anchor: وقد قال السدي في تفسيره، عن أبي مالك -وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس-وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r4.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r4.claim: The report says heaven was split into seven on Thursday and Friday, each heaven received its creatures and commands, the lowest was adorned with stars as protection from devils, and God then settled over the Throne.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214/r4.anchor: وقد قال السدي في تفسيره، عن أبي مالك -وعن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس-وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.claim: Ibn Salam says creation began Sunday: earths on Sunday and Monday, provisions and mountains Tuesday and Wednesday, heavens Thursday and Friday, with Adam created in the final hour of Friday, when the Hour will occur.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن سلام أنه قال: إن الله بدأ الخلق يوم الأحد، فخلق الأرضين في الأحد والاثنين،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says earth was created before heaven: smoke arose from it, and the seven heavens and seven earths were arranged one above another.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد في قوله: {هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا} قال: خلق الله الأرض قبل السماء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Qurʾanic passages establish that earth was created before heaven; he knows no scholarly disagreement except the reported exception of Qatada.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية دالة على أن الأرض خلقت قبل السماء، كما قال في آية السجدة:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.claim: Qatada is reported to have claimed that heaven was created before earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r4.anchor: إلا ما نقله ابن جرير عن قتادة: أنه زعم أن السماء خلقت قبل الأرض،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.speaker: القرطبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi hesitated over the order because al-Naziʿat mentions heaven's construction before earth's spreading.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r5.anchor: وقد توقف في ذلك القرطبي في تفسيره لقوله تعالى: {أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها * رفع سمكها فسواها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas answered that earth was created before heaven, but was spread out only after heaven's creation; Ibn Kathir notes that other exegetes give the same answer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r6.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري (1) : أن ابن عباس سئل عن هذا بعينه، فأجاب بأن الأرض خلقت قبل السماء وأن الأرض إنما دحيت بعد خلق السماء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir explains dahw as bringing out what earth held potentially once the earthly and heavenly forms were complete: waters emerged, plants grew, and the celestial orbits moved with their stars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p214#2/r7.anchor: ففسر الدحي بإخراج ما كان مودعا فيها بالقوة إلى الفعل لما اكتملت صورة المخلوقات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits from the Prophet a creation schedule: soil Saturday, mountains Sunday, trees Monday, harmful things Tuesday, light Wednesday, animals Thursday, and Adam late Friday.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: أخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بيدي فقال: "خلق الله التربة يوم السبت،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the report one of Sahih Muslim's strangest; ʿAli ibn al-Madini, al-Bukhari, and other critics attributed it to Kaʿb, saying a narrator mistook Kaʿb's report for a Prophetic one.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r2.anchor: وهذا الحديث من غرائب صحيح مسلم، وقد تكلم عليه علي بن المديني والبخاري وغير واحد من الحفاظ،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r3.speaker: علي بن المديني والبخاري وغيرهما
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r3.claim: The hadith critics treated the creation schedule as Kaʿb al-Ahbar's words, which Abu Hurayra had heard from Kaʿb, and said it was mistakenly raised to the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r3.anchor: تكلم عليه علي بن المديني والبخاري وغير واحد من الحفاظ، وجعلوه من كلام كعب،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r4.speaker: البيهقي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r4.claim: Al-Bayhaqi worked out the confusion that led some transmitters to misattribute the report to the Prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p215/r4.anchor: وإنما اشتبه على بعض الرواة فجعلوه (3) مرفوعا، وقد حرر ذلك البيهقي (4) .

JISHUMI:v1p305/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r7.claim: Jamʿ and ḍamm are near-synonyms; jamʿ is opposed to dispersal, and Friday and the place Jamʿ are named for gathering.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r7.anchor: الجمع والضم نظائر، ونقيض الجمع الفرق، ويقال: جمعه جمعا، وفرقه فرقا

JISHUMI:v1p305/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r8.claim: Gathering and separation are accidents in the genus of colors and indicate that bodies are originated.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r8.anchor: والاجتماع والافتراق عرضان من جنس الألوان، يدلان على حدث الجسم

JISHUMI:v1p305/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r9.claim: In Arabic, istawā can mean became straight, turned toward, gained control, or rose and ascended; this passage does not select one sense.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r9.anchor: والاستواء في اللغة ينصرف على أربعة أوجه: استوى: استقام، وهو الأصل

JISHUMI:v1p305/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r10.claim: Taswiya means straightening or adjusting; its essential sense is to make a thing even.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r10.anchor: والتسوية: التقويم، وحقيقتها جعل الشيء على الاستواء

JISHUMI:v1p305/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r11.claim: Sabʿ and sabʿa have feminine and masculine patterns respectively, though gender marking can depart from the regular pattern.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r11.anchor: والسبع للمؤنث، والسبعة للمذكر، وقد جاء التأنيث والتذكير على خلاف الأصل

JISHUMI:v1p305/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p305/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p305/r12.claim: ʿAlīm means knowing like ʿālim, but carries a stronger intensive force.
JISHUMI:v1p305/r12.anchor: وعليم: فعيل من علم، ومعناه عالم، غير أن في عليم مبالغة ليست في عالم

JISHUMI:v1p308/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p308/r1.claim: Some hold all such things to be prohibited, while others suspend judgment; the author says the verse confirms his own position.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r1.anchor: قوم: جميع ذلك على الحظر، وقال بعضهم: على التوقف، والآية تدل على صحة ما قلنا

JISHUMI:v1p308/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p308/r2.claim: God’s knowledge of everything refutes Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam’s claim that God knows created things through newly originated knowledge.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه تعالى عالم بكل شيء، فيبطل قول هشام بن الحكم

JISHUMI:v1p308/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p308/r3.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p308/r3.claim: Al-Aṣamm says that creating seven heavens from smoke demonstrates God’s power to resurrect the dead.
JISHUMI:v1p308/r3.anchor: قال الأصم: وتدل على البعث؛ لأن من قدر على خلق سبع سماوات من دخان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r10.claim: The created world benefits people in worldly life and religion: its design points to a wise Creator and recalls the afterlife, while it offers pleasures alongside dangers and hardships.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p151/r10.anchor: أما الانتفاع الدنيوي فظاهر واما الانتفاع الديني فالنظر فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r1.claim: Beneficial things not rationally prohibited were originally created lawful for anyone to take and use.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r1.anchor: على ان الأشياء التى يصح ان ينتفع بها ولم تجري مجرى المحظورات في العقل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r2.claim: The reading ‘the earth and what is in it’ works if earth means the lower regions, which include the globe, as heaven can mean the upper regions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r2.anchor: إن أراد بالأرض الجهات السفلية دون الغبراء كما تذكر السماء وتراد الجهات العلوية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r3.claim: جميعا is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the second relative pronoun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r3.anchor: نصب على الحال من الموصول الثاني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r4.claim: استوى means to become balanced and straight; استوى إلى is a metaphor for directing oneself straight toward something, without turning elsewhere.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r4.anchor: يقال استوى العود وغيره إذا قام واعتدل ثم قيل استوى اليه كالسهم المرسل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r5.claim: God turned toward heaven by will and intention after creating the earth’s contents, with no other creation intervening; heaven means the upper regions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152/r5.anchor: أي قصد اليها بإرادته ومشيئته بعد خلق ما في الأرض من غير ان يريد فيما بين ذلك خلق شيء آخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in فسواهن is vague and ‘seven heavens’ explains it, the more idiomatic Arabic construction; alternatives make it refer to heaven as a generic or pluralize سماة.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r1.anchor: تفسيره كقولهم ربه رجلا وقيل الضمير راجع إلى السماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.claim: Making the heavens level means ordering their creation and removing crookedness and flaws, or completing their creation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى تسويتهن تعديل خلقهن وتقديمه واخلاؤه من العوج والفطور أو إتمام خلقهن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.claim: God’s knowledge accounts for the heavens’ faultless, proportionate construction and for making earthly creation suit its inhabitants’ needs and interests.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r3.anchor: فمن ثم خلقهن خلقا مستويا محكما من غير تفاوت مع خلق ما في الأرض على حسب حاجات اهلها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.claim: ثم marks the difference in rank and the superiority of heaven’s creation, not elapsed time; even a temporal reading implies no intervening creation during the turning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r4.anchor: ههنا لما بين الخلقين من التفاوت وفضل خلق السموات على خلق الأرض لا للتراخي في الوقت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.claim: The use of ثم for rank rather than time is illustrated by ‘then he became one of those who believed.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p152#2/r5.anchor: ﴿ ثم كان من الذين آمنوا ﴾ البلد 17

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r1.claim: There is no conflict with the earth being spread after heaven’s creation: the earth’s substance was created earlier, but its spreading came later.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r1.anchor: لا لأن جرم الأرض تقدم خلقه خلق السماء واما دحوها فمتأخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r2.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says earth was first made at Jerusalem like a millstone with smoke clinging to it; the smoke rose to form the heavens, while the stone remained and the earth was spread from it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p153/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن خلق الله الأرض في موضع بيت المقدس كهيئة الفهر عليها دخان ملتزق بها ثم أصعد الدخان وخلق منه السموات

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes “turned to heaven” to mean that God turned toward it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r1.anchor: أي أقبل عليها , وهذا قول الفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.claim: A second explanation says God intended and directed Himself to create heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r2.anchor: معناه : عمد إليها , وقصد إلى خلقها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.speaker: المفضل
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal says God’s action turned toward heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r3.anchor: والثالث : أن فعل الله تحول إلى السماء , وهو قول المفضل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.speaker: الحسن البصري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī takes it to mean that God’s command and work directed toward heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r4.anchor: معناه : ثم استوى أمره وصنعه الذي صنع به الأشياء إلى السماء , وهذا قول الحسن البصري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r5.claim: Another explanation says that the heaven became level or rose through Him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.claim: Al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas takes istiwāʾ as rising and loftiness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r6.anchor: وممن قال بذلك : الربيع بن أنس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.claim: Those who read it as rising differ over whether the one rising is the Creator, who made heaven, or the smoke God made into heaven.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p92#2/r7.anchor: ثم اختلف قائلو هذا التأويل في الذي استوى إلى السماء فعلا عليها على قولين : أحدهما : أنه خالقها ومنشئها . والثاني : أنه الدخان

MUQATIL:2:28-29/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r5.claim: God created everything on earth for people; then He began creating the heavens and formed them as seven heavens.
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r5.anchor: { هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا } من شئ { ثم استوى إلى السمآء } فبدأ بخلقهن،

MUQATIL:2:28-29/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r6.claim: The creation of the heavens and earth is greater than creating people, as stated in 40:57.
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r6.anchor: فهذا أعظم من خلق الإنسان، وذلك قوله سبحانه:

MUQATIL:2:28-29/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r7.claim: God knows every created thing, including resurrection and everything else.
MUQATIL:2:28-29/r7.anchor: { وهو بكل شيء } من الخلق { عليم } [آية: 29] بالبعث وغيره.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r1.claim: God created earthly things for worldly and religious benefit: their marvels disclose a wise Creator, and pleasures and hardships recall afterlife reward and punishment.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r1.anchor: أى لأجلكم ولا نتفاعكم به فى دنياكم ودينكم اما الأول فظاهر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r2.speaker: الكرخي وأبو بكر الرازي والمعتزلة
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r2.claim: Al-Karkhi, Abu Bakr al-Razi, and the Muʿtazila infer that beneficial things were originally permissible from God’s creating them for people.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r2.anchor: وقد استدل الكرخى و أبو بكر الرازي والمعتزلة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r3.claim: جميعا is an accusative circumstantial qualifier of ما.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r3.anchor: ﴿ جميعا ﴾ نصب على الحال من ما

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r4.claim: استوى means becoming straight and upright; with إلى it means directly intending the heavens without turning aside.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r4.anchor: الاستواء الاعتدال والاستقامة يقال استوى العود أى قام واعتدل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r5.claim: السماء here means the upper directions, so استوى إليها means turned toward what is above.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r5.anchor: والمراد بالسماء جهات العلو كأنه قيل ثم استوى إلى فوق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r6.claim: The pronoun هنّ is ambiguous and explained by سبع سماوات, or refers to السماء, a singular used generically with plural meaning.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r7.claim: Making the heavens even means either removing crookedness and fissures or completing their creation.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r8.claim: Thumma marks the greater rank of creating the heavens. This does not conflict with 79:30: earth’s body came first but its spreading came later.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r8.anchor: لأن جرم الأرض تقدم خلقه خلق السماء وأما دحوها فمتأخر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r9.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r9.claim: Al-Hasan describes earth at Jerusalem as a stone-like mass with clinging smoke; God raised the smoke to form the heavens, kept the mass in place, and spread earth from it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r9.anchor: وعن الحسن خلق الله الأرض فى موضع بيت المقدس كهيئة الفهر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r11.claim: God made the heavens perfectly and ordered earthly creation according to its inhabitants’ needs and benefits.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r11.anchor: فمن ثم خلقهن خلقا مستويا محكما من غير تفاوت

NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو وعلي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r12.claim: The segment contrasts a Medinan reading except Warsh with Abu ʿAmr and ʿAli, who treat the waw in وهو and its sisters as part of the word, like عضد.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p35#3/r12.anchor: وهو وأخواته مدنى غير ورش وهو هو و أبو عمرو وعلى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r1.claim: خلق means bringing something into existence after nonexistence; it can also be used of a person making something, as illustrated by a cited poetic line.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r1.anchor: { خلق } معناه اخترع وأوجد بعد العدم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r2.speaker: ابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r2.claim: Ibn Kaysān explains لكم as من أجلكم, meaning for your sake.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r2.anchor: وقال ابن كيسان: { خلق لكم } أي من أجلكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r3.claim: One explanation is that everything in the earth is bestowed for human benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r3.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أن جميع ما في الأرض منعم به عليكم فهو لكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r4.claim: Another explanation sees the verse as evidence for monotheism and reflection; Qurtubi says this is the correct view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنه دليل على التوحيد والاعتبار. قلت: وهذا هو الصحيح على ما نبينه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r5.claim: The phrase may also mean all the things people need.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون عنى به ما هم إليه محتاجون من جميع الأشياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r6.claim: Those who hold that useful things are originally permitted cite this verse and 45:13, arguing that pleasant foods were not created pointlessly: their benefit must be for humans, whether through taste, abstention as a test, or reflection, and those benefits require tasting them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r6.anchor: استدل من قال إن أصل الأشياء التي ينتفع بها الإباحة بهذه الآية وما كان مثلها كقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r7.claim: Qurtubi rejects that argument: God is not obligated to create for benefit; the proposed benefits are not exhaustive or dependent on tasting, other signs can reveal tastes, and some items may be lethal poisons; the argument also faces prohibitionists’ counterarguments.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r7.anchor: وهذا فاسد لأنا لا نسلم لزوم العبث من خلقها إلا لمنفعة، بل خلقها كذلك لأنه لا يجب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r8.speaker: المعتزلة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r8.claim: Qurtubi attributes the three positions—original permission, prohibition, and suspension until revelation—to the Muʿtazila; the suspension argument says an act not known as good or bad might be good in itself, so judgment must wait for revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r8.anchor: وتوقف آخرون وقالوا: ما من فعل لا ندرك منه حسنا ولا قبحا إلا ويمكن أن يكون حسنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r9.speaker: أبو الحسن وأصحابه وأكثر المالكية والصيرفي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r9.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan, his companions, most Mālikīs, and al-Ṣayrafī explicitly hold suspension: there is no ruling before revelation, revelation may rule as it wills, and reason itself neither obligates nor forbids.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r9.anchor: وقد أطلق الشيخ أبو الحسن وأصحابه وأكثر المالكية والصيرفي في هذه المسألة القول بالوقف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r10.speaker: ابن الصائغ
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r10.claim: As Ibn ʿAṭiyya transmits from Ibn Furak, Ibn al-Ṣāʾigh says reason was never without revealed guidance: every case has a report, an applicable basis, or a continuing default, making separate inquiry into prohibition, permission, or suspension unnecessary.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r10.anchor: وحكى ابن فورك عن ابن الصائغ أنه قال: لم يخل العقل قط من السمع، ولا نازلة إلا وفيها سمع،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r11.claim: Qurtubi says the correct sense of creating what is on earth is to prompt reflection: the surrounding signs of life, death, creation, and the fashioned heavens show that the creator can also resurrect people.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29/r11.anchor: الصحيح في معنى قوله تعالى: { خلق لكم ما في الأرض } الاعتبار. يدل عليه ما قبله وما بعده من نصب العبر:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.claim: If لكم means benefit, Qurtubi says the benefit here is reflection: even scorpions and snakes can remind people of Hell’s punishment and prompt faith and avoidance of sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r1.anchor: فإن قيل: إن معنى «لكم» الانتفاع أي لتنتفعوا بجميع ذلك قلنا: المراد بالانتفاع الاعتبار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the verse implies neither prohibition, permission, nor suspension; it occurs as proof and reminder of God’s oneness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وليس في الإخبار بهذه القدرة عن هذه الجملة ما يقتضي حظرا ولا إباحة ولا وقفا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.speaker: أرباب المعاني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.claim: The spiritual commentators say earthly things were created to strengthen people for obedience, not to direct them toward disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r3.anchor: وقال أرباب المعاني في قوله: { خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا } لتتقووا به على طاعته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.speaker: أبو عثمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿUthmān says the gift of all things and their subjection should reveal God’s generosity, reassure people of His promised reward in the Hereafter, and keep them from deeming His abundant favor excessive for little work, since He began with the great gift of monotheism.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان: وهب لك الكل وسخره لك لتستدل به على سعة جوده، وتسكن إلى ما ضمن لك من جزيل عطائه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r5.claim: A man asked the Prophet for help; the Prophet said he had nothing but invited him to buy on credit until provision came. Umar objected that the Prophet should not commit what he could not pay; an Anṣārī urged him to spend without fearing shortage, the Prophet smiled, and said he had been commanded to do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r5.anchor: روى زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه. " أن رجلا أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r6.claim: The scholars say fear of shortage reflects bad opinion of God: He created earthly provisions for Adam’s children and subjected them to people as proof and to remove their excuse, so that they might serve Him as created.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r6.anchor: قال علماؤنا رحمة الله عليهم: فخوف الإقلال من سوء الظن بالله لأن الله تعالى خلق الأرض بما فيها لولد آدم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r7.claim: A person who trusts God need not fear poverty, since God replaces what is spent and is generous.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#2/r7.anchor: فإذا كان العبد حسن الظن بالله لم يخف الإقلال لأنه يخلف عليه كما قال تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.claim: A divine report says God’s mercy precedes His anger and He tells Adam’s child to spend, promising provision; His hand is full and giving continuously without depletion through night or day.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r1.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.claim: The Prophet says two angels descend each morning: one asks God to replace what the spender gives, the other asks that the miser suffer loss; the same call is made at sunset, and Qurtubi says the reports are sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r2.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما من يوم يصبح العباد فيه إلا وملكان ينزلان فيقول أحدهما اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r3.claim: One who knows God’s wealth and generosity gives without fear; likewise the person content with minimal sustenance and detached from worldly desire gives in ease or hardship, while those still desiring future goods fear that giving now will leave them short later.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r3.anchor: فمن استنار صدره، وعلم غنى ربه وكرمه أنفق ولم يخف الإقلال وكذلك من ماتت شهواته عن الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet told Asmāʾ to give and not count or hoard, lest God withhold or count against her.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r4.anchor:
روى مسلم
" عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر قالت: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «انفحي أو انضحي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r5.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r5.claim: Al-Nasāʾī reports that when ʿĀʾisha gave a petitioner something and inspected it, the Prophet asked whether she wanted nothing to enter or leave her house without her knowledge; he told her not to count lest God count against her.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r5.anchor:
وروى النسائي
" عن عائشة قالت: دخل علي سائل مرة وعندي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فأمرت له بشيء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.claim: ثم orders the report or discourse, not the events themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r6.anchor: «ثم» لترتيب الإخبار لا لترتيب الأمر في نفسه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.claim: In Arabic, استوى can mean to rise or ascend over something; Qurtubi cites 23:28, 43:13, and a poem in which a star rises high.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r7.anchor: والاستواء في اللغة: الارتفاع والعلو على الشيء قال الله تعالى: فإذا استويت أنت ومن معك على الفلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.claim: Qurtubi calls this verse and similar passages among the difficult texts and says interpreters take three approaches.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r8.anchor: وهذه الآية من المشكلات، والناس فيها وفيما شاكلها على ثلاثة أوجه،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.claim: Qurtubi cites God’s promise to replace what people spend and His description of Himself as rich and generous, quoting 34:39 and 27:40.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#3/r9.anchor: ومآ أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r1.claim: One approach reads and affirms the verse without interpreting it, as many imams do; Mālik says the meaning of istiwāʾ is known, its modality inconceivable, belief obligatory, and questioning it an innovation, and orders the questioner removed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r1.anchor: قال مالك: الاستواء غير مجهول، والكيف غير معقول، والإيمان به واجب، والسؤال عنه بدعة، وأراك رجل سوء!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r2.speaker: المشبهة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r2.claim: A second approach reads and interprets the verse according to the apparent sense of the language; Qurtubi identifies this as the position of the anthropomorphists.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: نقرؤها ونفسرها على ما يحتمله ظاهر اللغة. وهذا قول المشبهة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r3.claim: A third approach reads the verse and gives it a figurative interpretation that rules out its apparent sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: نقرؤها ونتأولها ونحيل حملها على ظاهرها.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r4.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r4.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives Arabic uses of istiwāʾ for reaching maturity or becoming straight, and for turning or directing oneself toward someone; he explains the verse as God turning toward the heaven and notes Ibn ʿAbbās’s reported gloss صعد.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء في قوله عز وجل: { ثم استوى إلى السمآء فسواهن } قال: الاستواء في كلام العرب على وجهين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r5.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r5.claim: Al-Bayhaqī accepts istiwāʾ as turning toward: it means intending to create the heaven, and intention is a permissible divine attribute; ثم relates to creation, not intention.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r5.anchor: وقال البيهقي أبو بكر أحمد بن علي بن الحسين: قوله: «استوى» بمعنى أقبل صحيح،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r6.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqī says Ibn ʿAbbās’s transmitted gloss was taken from al-Kalbī’s tafsir, and al-Kalbī is weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r6.anchor: وأما ما حكي عن ابن عباس فإنما أخذه عن تفسير الكلبي، والكلبي ضعيف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r7.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة وابن كيسان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r7.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna and Ibn Kaysān say God قصد إليها, meaning He directed Himself toward it by creating and originating it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r7.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة وابن كيسان في قوله: { ثم استوى إلى السمآء }: قصد إليها،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r8.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r8.claim: Another interpretation affirms the verse without specifying modality or limit; al-Ṭabarī chooses this position.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r8.anchor: وقيل: على دون تكييف ولا تحديد واختاره الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r9.speaker: أبو العالية الرياحي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r9.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya al-Riyāḥī says istiwāʾ means rising; al-Bayhaqī understands him to mean the elevation of God’s command, associated with the water vapor from which the heaven was made.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r9.anchor: ويذكر عن أبي العالية الرياحي في هذه الآية أنه يقال: استوى بمعنى أنه ارتفع.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r10.claim: Some say the thing raised is the smoke, but Ibn ʿAṭiyya objects that this is incompatible with the wording of the verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r10.anchor: وقيل: إن المستوي الدخان. وقال ابن عطية: وهذا يأباه وصف الكلام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r11.claim: Another interpretation takes استوى as استولى, supported by a poem about Bishr ruling Iraq without sword or blood; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this usage applies to 20:5.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#4/r11.anchor: وقيل: المعنى استولى كما قال الشاعر: قد استوى بشر على العراق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r1.claim: Qurtubi’s rule for this verse and similar ones is to deny motion and change of place.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r1.anchor: والقاعدة في هذه الآية ونحوها منع الحركة والنقلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r2.claim: The verse appears to put the creation of earth before heaven, as does Sūrat Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda; 79:27–30 describes heaven’s building before the earth’s spreading, and 6:1 says God created both heavens and earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r2.anchor: يظهر من هذه الآية أنه سبحانه خلق الأرض قبل السماء وكذلك في «حم السجدة». وقال في النازعات: أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r3.claim: Qatāda holds that heaven was created first, as al-Ṭabarī transmits.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r3.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة: إن السماء خلقت أولا حكاه عنه الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r4.speaker: مجاهد وغيره من المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r4.claim: Mujāhid and other exegetes say God dried the water beneath His Throne into earth, raised vapor from it to make heaven, then fashioned seven heavens and spread out the earth, which had not yet been spread.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره من المفسرين: إنه تعالى أيبس الماء الذي كان عرشه عليه، فجعله أرضا وثار منه دخان فارتفع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r5.claim: Qurtubi reconciles Qatāda’s view: heaven’s vapor was created first, then earth, then God fashioned the vapor into heaven, and spread the earth afterward.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r5.anchor: وقول قتادة يخرج على وجه صحيح إن شاء الله تعالى، وهو أن الله تعالى خلق أولا دخان السماء ثم خلق الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r6.claim: A report transmitted through al-Suddī’s authorities says the Throne was on water and nothing preceded water; God drew smoke from it, raised and named it heaven, dried the water into one earth, then split it into seven earths over Sunday and Monday.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#5/r6.anchor: عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود، وعن ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r1.speaker: author
