QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r1.claim: A cosmological account puts the earth on a fish, with water, a rock, and a king above it; when the fish shakes the earth trembles until mountains fix it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r1.anchor: والحوت في الماء و الماء على صفاة، والصفاة على ظهر ملك،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r2.claim: The earth’s mountains, provisions, trees, and needs were made over Tuesday and Wednesday, within four days including the first two.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r2.anchor: وخلق الجبال فيها، وأقوات أهلها وشجرها، وما ينبغي لها في يومين، في الثلاثاء والأربعاء،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r3.claim: The heavens began as smoke from water vapor, first one heaven and then seven split from it on Thursday and Friday; Friday was named because creation was gathered then.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r3.anchor: وكان ذلك الدخان من تنفس الماء حين تنفس فجعلها سماء واحدة، ثم فتقها فجعلها سبع سموات في يومين، في الخميس والجمعة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r4.claim: God made inhabitants and features in each heaven, adorned the lowest with stars as ornament and protection from devils, and ascended the Throne after creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r4.anchor: فجعلها زينة وحفظا تحفظ من الشياطين. فلما فرغ من خلق ما أحب استوى على العرش

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r5.claim: In a report through Wakiʿ, al-Aʿmash, and Abu Zibyan, Ibn ʿAbbas says the pen first wrote destiny through the Resurrection; then the fish bore earth, vapor split the heavens, and mountains steadied earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: إن أول ما خلق الله عز وجل من شيء «القلم» فقال له اكتب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r6.claim: Although the Ibn ʿAbbas report reverses the order by putting earth before vapor, al-Qurtubi prefers the first account because the earth was spread afterward; he says speculation cannot settle this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#6/r6.anchor: والرواية الأولى عنه وعن غيره أولى لقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r1.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r1.claim: Kaʿb al-Ahbar says Iblis urged the fish Lūthiyā to shake off earth and its inhabitants; God sent a creature into the fish’s nostril, and it sought refuge from it, so earth was spared.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r1.anchor: وذكر أبو نعيم عن كعب الأحبار أن إبليس تغلغل إلى الحوت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet says everything was created from water, then advises feeding, greeting, kinship, and night prayer for peaceful entry to Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قلت: يا رسول الله، إذا رأيتك طابت نفسي وقرت عيني، أنبئني عن كل شيء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r3.claim: Abu Hatim explains Abu Hurayra’s request for knowledge of everything as asking about everything created from water.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r3.anchor: قال أبو حاتم قول أبي هريرة:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports Ibn ʿAbbas saying the Prophet called the pen the first thing God created and ordered it to write all future events.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يحدث أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «إن أول شيء خلقه الله القلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r5.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r5.claim: The report that the Prophet called the pen the first creation is also transmitted from ʿUbada ibn al-Samit in a marfuʿ form.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r5.anchor: ويروى ذلك أيضا عن عبادة بن الصامت مرفوعا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r6.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r6.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says the pen was first after water, wind, and the Throne, consistent with the report that heavens and earth were then created.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r6.anchor: قال البيهقي: وإنما أراد والله أعلم أول شيء خلقه بعد خلق الماء والريح والعرش «القلم».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r7.claim: Tawus reports Ibn ʿAmr answering that creation came from water, light, darkness, wind, and earth, but he does not know their origin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r7.anchor: عن طاوس قال: جاء رجل إلى عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص فسأله: مم خلق الخلق؟ قال: من الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r8.claim: Tawus says Ibn al-Zubayr gave the same answer as Ibn ʿAmr about creation’s elements.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r8.anchor: ثم أتى الرجل عبد الله بن الزبير فسأله فقال مثل قول عبد الله بن عمرو.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r9.claim: Tawus likewise reports Ibn ʿAbbas naming water, light, darkness, wind, and earth as creation’s sources; he then cites a verse to explain their source.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#7/r9.anchor: فأتى الرجل عبد الله بن عباس فسأله فقال: مم خلق الخلق؟ قال: من الماء والنور والظلمة والريح والتراب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas cites God subjecting the heavens and earth to explain that all originate in God’s creative act.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r1.anchor: وسخر لكم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض جميعا منه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r2.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqi interprets “from Him” as God’s creative act: He created water first, or water and whatever He willed without prior material or model, then made it a basis for later creation; He alone creates.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r2.anchor: قال البيهقي: أراد أن مصدر الجميع منه، أي من خلقه وإبداعه واختراعه. خلق الماء أولا،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r3.claim: The heavens are explicitly seven; the earth’s count is unambiguous only in 65:12.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r3.anchor: ذكر تعالى أن السموات سبع. ولم يأت للأرض في التنزيل عدد صريح لا يحتمل التأويل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r4.claim: One view reads “their like” as matching the heavens in number, though earths differ in observed qualities.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r4.anchor: فقيل: ومن الأرض مثلهن أي في العدد لأن الكيفية والصفة مختلفة بالمشاهدة والأخبار فتعين العدد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r5.claim: Another view takes “their like” to mean earths’ thickness and the distances between them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r5.anchor: وقيل: ومن الأرض مثلهن [الطلاق: 12] أي في غلظهن وما بينهن.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r6.speaker: الداودي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r6.claim: Al-Dawudi says there are seven earths, not split apart from one another.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r6.anchor: وقيل: هي سبع إلا أنه لم يفتق بعضها من بعض قاله الداودي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi prefers the first view: seven earths like the seven heavens.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r7.anchor: والصحيح الأول وأنها سبع كالسموات سبع.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r8.claim: Muslim reports the Prophet warning that whoever unjustly takes a handspan of land will be encircled by seven earths.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r8.anchor: روى مسلم عن سعيد بن زيد قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r9.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r9.claim: Aisha transmits the same warning with “from seven earths” instead of “to seven earths.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r9.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها مثله، إلا أن فيه «من» بدل «إلى».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r10.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet’s warning that whoever takes land unjustly is encircled by seven earths on Judgment Day.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r11.claim: Al-Nasaʾi reports Moses asking for a special invocation; God teaches him the declaration of divine unity, which outweighs seven heavens and earths.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r11.anchor: روى النسائي عن أبي سعيد الخدري عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r12.claim: Al-Tirmidhi’s long report describes the cloud, protected heaven, distances of five hundred years between levels, seven heavens and earths, and the Throne.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#8/r12.anchor: وروى الترمذي عن أبي هريرة قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r1.speaker: أبو عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhi’s Abu ʿIsa explains “fall upon God” as reaching God’s knowledge, power, and dominion: His knowledge and power are everywhere while He is above the Throne.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r1.anchor: قال أبو عيسى: قراءة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الآية تدل على أنه أراد: لهبط على علم الله وقدرته وسلطانه،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r2.speaker: أبو عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi calls the report gharīb and notes that al-Hasan did not hear it from Abu Hurayra.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r2.anchor: قال: هذا حديث غريب، والحسن لم يسمع من أبي هريرة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r3.claim: A report through Abu al-Duha attributes to Ibn ʿAbbas the claim that each earth has a prophet and counterparts to Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Jesus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r3.anchor: وقد روى أبو الضحى واسمه مسلم عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r4.speaker: البيهقي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r4.claim: Al-Bayhaqi calls the chain sound but the report extremely anomalous, with no evidence for Abu al-Duha’s claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r4.anchor: قال البيهقي: إسناد هذا عن ابن عباس صحيح، وهو شاذ بمرة لا أعلم لأبي الضحا عليه دليلا والله أعلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r5.claim: The opening clause is a subject-predicate construction; ma is accusative and, for Sibawayh, jamiʿan is circumstantial.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r5.anchor: ابتداء وخبر. «ما» في موضع نصب. { جميعا } عند سيبويه نصب على الحال.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r6.speaker: أهل نجد وأهل الحجاز
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r6.claim: Najd speakers use imāla on istawā to indicate a yāʾ root; Hijaz speakers use tafkhīm.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r6.anchor: أهل نجد يميلون ليدلوا على أنه من ذوات الياء، وأهل الحجاز يفخمون.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r7.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r7.claim: Al-Nahhas parses “seven” as an appositive to the pronoun in “them” or as object of an implied verb, “He levels seven heavens.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r7.anchor: سبع } منصوب على البدل من الهاء والنون أي فسوى سبع سموات. ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا على تقدير يسوي بينهن سبع سموات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r8.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash instead parses “seven” as a circumstantial accusative.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r9.claim: The final clause is subject-predicate; huwa’s hāʾ is originally vocalized, while sukūn eases pronunciation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r9.anchor: وهو بكل شيء عليم } ابتداء وخبر. والأصل في «هو» تحريك الهاء، والإسكان استخفاف.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r10.speaker: الأخفش والزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash derives samāʾ as a plural of samāwa, al-Zajjaj from samāʾa; samāwāt and samāʾāt are plural forms, and sawāhun treats heaven as plural or generic singular.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r10.anchor: وتكون جمعا لسماوة في قول الأخفش، وسماءة في قول الزجاج، وجمع الجمع سماوات وسماءات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r11.claim: Sawāhun can mean smoothing the heavens’ surfaces or making them equal.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r11.anchor: ومعنى سواهن سوى سطوحهن بالإملاس. وقيل: جعلهن سواء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r12.claim: Since God creates all things, He knows them all; His knowledge is one eternal attribute subsisting in His essence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r12.anchor: فهو العالم والعليم بجميع المعلومات بعلم قديم أزلي واحد قائم بذاته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r13.speaker: المعتزلة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r13.claim: The Muʿtazila affirm God is knowing but deny a distinct attribute of knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r13.anchor: ووافقنا المعتزلة على العالمية دون العلمية.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r14.speaker: الجهمية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r14.claim: The Jahmiyya say God is knowing without knowledge subsisting in a locus; al-Qurtubi rejects this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#9/r14.anchor: وقالت الجهمية: عالم بلا علم قائم لا في محل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r1.claim: Al-Qurtubi cites verses on revelation, judgment, pregnancy, and the unseen occurring with God’s knowledge; fuller proof of this and other attributes is deferred to 2:185.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r1.anchor: وما تحمل من أنثى ولا تضع إلا بعلمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r2.speaker: الكسائي وقالون عن نافع وأبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r2.claim: Al-Kisaʾi, Qalun from Nafiʿ, and Abu ʿAmr (except before thumma) silence hāʾ in huwa and hiya after fa, waw, lam, or thumma; other readers vocalize it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r2.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وقالون عن نافع بإسكان الهاء من: هو وهي، إذا كان قبلها فاء أو واو أو لام أو ثم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r3.speaker: أبو عون عن الحلواني عن قالون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r3.claim: Abu ʿAwn, through al-Hulwani from Qalun, also reads the hāʾ quiescent in an yamla huwa.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:29#10/r3.anchor: وزاد أبو عون عن الحلواني عن قالون إسكان الهاء من { أن يمل هو } ، والباقون بالتحريك.

QASHANI:2:28-29/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r6.claim: Everything on earth means the lower elemental realm, source and material of human creation, existence, and continuance.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r6.anchor: الجهة السفلية التي هي العالم العنصري جميعا لكونها مبادئ خلقكم ومواد وجودكم

QASHANI:2:28-29/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r7.claim: The turn to the upper realm marks the difference between realms and creative acts, not a time gap that would put earth before heaven.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r7.anchor: وثم للتفاوت بين الجهتين والإيجادين الإبداعي والتكويني لا للتراخي بين الزمانين

QASHANI:2:28-29/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r8.claim: On the common outward account, the apparent Throne and Footstool are the eighth and ninth.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r8.anchor: فعدلهن سبع سموات بحسب ما تراه العامة، إذ الثمن والتاسع هو الكرسي والعرش الظاهران

QASHANI:2:28-29/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r9.claim: Inwardly the lower realm is bodily, like a body, while heaven is the higher-ranking spiritual world; the transition distinguishes creation from command.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r9.anchor: الحقيقة أن الجهة السفلية هي العالم الجسماني كالبدن وأعضائه لدنو رتبته

QASHANI:2:28-29/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r10.claim: The seven heavens signify levels: earthly malakut, psychic powers and jinn, then soul, heart, intellect, secret, spirit, and hidden spiritual secret.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r10.anchor: الأول: هو عالم الملكوت الأرضية والقوى النفسانية والجن.

QASHANI:2:28-29/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r11.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
QASHANI:2:28-29/r11.claim: ʿAlī says he knows heaven's paths better than earth's; these paths are states and stations such as asceticism, trust, and contentment.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r11.anchor: وإلى هذا أشار أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام بقوله:

QASHANI:2:28-29/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:28-29/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:28-29/r12.claim: Terminology differs: philosophers call spirit what Sufis call intellect; the Sufi intellect here is the rational soul's faculty, while the heart is the rational soul illuminated by spirit.
QASHANI:2:28-29/r12.anchor: العقل باصطلاح الحكمة هو الروح باصطلاح أهل التصوف

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r1.claim: This is the second universal blessing; the order follows human need, since benefit from earth and sky comes only after life.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r1.anchor: هذا هو النعمة الثانية التي عمت المكلفين بأسرهم وما أحسن ما رعى الله سبحانه وتعالى هذا الترتيب

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r2.claim: Rāzī refers back to his explanation of “who created you” in 2:21.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r2.anchor: أما قوله : { خلق } فقد مر تفسيره في قوله : { اعبدوا ربكم الذى خلقكم }

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r3.claim: “For you” indicates benefits for religious and worldly life: bodily well-being and strength for worship, and reflection on created things as evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r3.anchor: وأما قوله : { لكم } فهو يدل على أن المذكور بعد قوله خلق لأجل انتفاعنا في الدين والدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r4.claim: “Everything on earth” gathers benefits from animals, plants, minerals, mountains, crafts, and things human reason has devised.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r4.anchor: جميع المنافع ، فمنها ما يتصل بالحيوان والنبات والمعادن

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r5.claim: Rāzī connects the verse to God’s subjection of what is in the heavens and earth for people.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r5.anchor: كما قال : { وسخر لكم ما فى * السماوات وما في الارض }

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r6.claim: The sequence can be read as two grounds for rebuke: God gave life, and He created everything in earth and sky for human benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r6.anchor: فكأنه سبحانه وتعالى قال كيف تكفرون بالله وكنتم أمواتا فأحياكم وكيف تكفرون بالله وقد خلق لكم ما في السموات

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r7.claim: The creation of the earth’s contents also argues against denying resurrection: the One who created them for people is able to restore them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r7.anchor: أو يقال كيف تكفرون بقدرة الله على الإعادة وقد أحياكم بعد موتكم

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r8.claim: Rāzī points to other passages detailing these benefits, including the pouring of rain and the creation of livestock.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r8.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى ذكر تفاصيل هذه المنافع في سورة مختلفة كما قال : { أنا صببنا الماء صبا } وقال

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r9.claim: Rāzī’s Ashʿarite position is that God does not act for an end that would perfect Him, since completion through another would imply prior deficiency.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r9.anchor: قال أصحابنا : إنه سبحانه وتعالى لا يفعل فعلا لغرض لأنه لو كان كذلك كان مستكملا بذلك الغرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r10.claim: If an act’s goal benefits another, that benefit either is preferable to God’s own benefit, implying He gains from it, or is not preferable, leaving no motive to secure it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r10.anchor: فإن كان أولى فهو تعالى قد انتفع بذلك الفعل فيعود المحذور المذكور وإن كان الثاني لم يكن تحصيل ذلك الغرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r11.claim: Acting for a goal would imply inability to attain it except through that act, which is impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r11.anchor: وثانيها : أن من فعل فعلا لغرض كان عاجزا عن تحصيل ذلك الغرض إلا بواسطة ذلك الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r12.claim: If the goal were eternal, the act would be eternal; if created, God would make it for another goal, producing an impossible infinite regress.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r12.anchor: وثالثها : أنه تعالى لو فعل فعلا لغرض لكان ذلك الغرض إن كان قديما لزم قدم الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r13.claim: If divine action depended on serving human welfare, God would not impose a harmful burden on those He knows will not believe, yet He does.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r13.anchor: ورابعها : أنه تعالى لو كان يفعل لغرض لكان ذلك الغرض هو رعاية مصلحة المكلفين

RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r14.claim: Rāzī explains purpose-language in “for you” and “except to worship Me” analogically: God does what would count as goal-directed if another did it.
RAZI-FULL:v2p141#2/r14.anchor: أطلق الله عليه لفظ الغرض بسبب هذه المشابهة

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r1.claim: The verse implies that God is not needy; if He needed these things, He would have created them for Himself as well as for others.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r1.anchor: قوله : { خلق لكم ما فى الأرض جميعا } يقتضي أنه لا تصح الحاجة على الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r2.speaker: أهل الإباحة
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r2.claim: The permissivists infer that because God created everything on earth for everyone, no one can have an exclusive claim to anything.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r2.anchor: احتج أهل الإباحة بقوله تعالى : { خلق لكم ما فى الأرض جميعا } على أنه تعالى خلق الكل

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r3.claim: Rāzī rejects that inference: the collective wording pairs the whole with the whole and individuals with individuals, while separate evidence determines ownership.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r3.anchor: وهو ضعيف لأنه تعالى قابل الكل بالكل ، فيقتضي مقابلة الفرد بالفرد ، والتعيين يستفاد

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r4.claim: Jurists use the verse to establish that the default rule for benefits is permissibility.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r4.anchor: والفقهاء رحمهم الله استدلوا به على أن الأصل في المنافع الإباحة

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r5.claim: Some infer that eating clay is forbidden because God created what is in the earth for people, not the earth itself.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r5.anchor: قيل إنها تدل على حرمة أكل الطين لأنه تعالى خلق لنا ما في الأرض دون نفس الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r6.claim: Rāzī answers that things located within the earth include minerals and its veins, and mention of one thing does not exclude what is unmentioned.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r6.anchor: وكذلك عروق الأرض وما يجري مجرى بعض لها ولأن تخصيص الشيء بالذكر لا يدل على نفي الحكم عما عداه

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r7.claim: Istiwāʾ can mean standing upright or straightening, but that bodily sense cannot apply to God.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r7.anchor: الاستواء في كلام العرب قد يكون بمعنى الانتصاب وضده الإعوجاج ولما كان ذلك من صفات الأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r8.claim: Rāzī rejects spatial elevation: it would already exist before earth’s creation, contradicting thumma, which marks a later sequence here.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r8.anchor: ولو كان المراد من هذا الاستواء العلو

RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r9.claim: He interprets the phrase as turning directly toward or intending the sky, like a straight arrow aimed without distraction, and creating it after earth.
RAZI-FULL:v2p142/r9.anchor: استوى إليه كالسهم المرسل إذا قصده قصدا مستويا من غير أن يلتفت إلى شيء آخر

RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r1.claim: Rāzī reads 41:9–10 as two days for earth, two more for its provisions, then two for heaven, totaling the six days mentioned elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r1.anchor: مفسر بقوله : { قل * أئنكم * لتكفرون بالذي خلق الأرض في يومين وتجعلون له

RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r2.speaker: بعض الملحدة
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r2.claim: Some critics see a chronology conflict: 2:29 and 41:9–10 place earth before heaven, while 79:27–30 appears to place earth after heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r2.anchor: قال بعض الملحدة هذه الآية تدل على أن خلق الأرض قبل خلق السماء وكذا قوله

RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r3.speaker: العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r3.claim: One scholarly answer distinguishes creating earth from spreading it: earth was created first, then spread after the sky was made.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r3.anchor: أحدها : يجوز أن يكون خلق الأرض قبل خلق السماء إلا أنه ما دحاها حتى خلق السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r4.claim: Rāzī objects that earth’s physical body cannot be separated from its spreading, and that creating everything in it before heaven requires it already to have been spread.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r4.anchor: أن الأرض جسم عظيم فامتنع انفكاك خلقها عن التدحية وإذا كانت التدحية متأخرة عن خلق السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r5.claim: A reply says 79:30 delays only earth’s spreading, not its creation, until after the sky’s creation.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r5.anchor: والجواب : أن قوله تعالى : { والأرض بعد ذلك دحاها } يقتضي تقديم خلق السماء على الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r6.claim: Rāzī responds that 79:27–30 places the sky’s creation and leveling before earth’s spreading; if spreading accompanies earth’s substance, the difficulty returns.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r6.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : قوله تعالى : { أشد خلقا أم السماء

RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r7.claim: Rāzī’s preferred solution is that thumma enumerates blessings rather than chronology, so what is mentioned later may have occurred earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143/r7.anchor: وثالثها : وهو الجواب الصحيح أن قوله : ( ثم ) ليس للترتيب ههنا وإنما هو على جهة تعديد النعم

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r1.claim: The pronoun in فسواهن is initially indeterminate, with سبع سماوات explaining it, as in ربه رجلا; this is the more idiomatic Arabic construction.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r1.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : الضمير في فسواهن ضمير مبهم ، وسبع سموات تفسير له كقوله ربه رجلا

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r2.claim: Deferring the explanation makes the object seem grander, awakens curiosity, and then satisfies it when the explanation arrives.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r2.anchor: لأنه إذا أبهم تشوفت النفوس إلى الاطلاع عليه وفي البيان بعد ذلك شفاء لها بعد التشوف

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r3.claim: An alternate analysis returns the pronoun to السماء, treating it either as a generic noun or as the singular جمع سماءة; Razi favors the first analysis as better Arabic.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r3.anchor: وقيل الضمير راجع إلى السماء ، والسماء في معنى الجنس وقيل جمع سماءة

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r4.claim: To make the heavens proportionate is to complete their creation and remove crookedness and flaws.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى تسويتهن تعديل خلقهن وإخلاؤه من العوج والفطور وإتمام خلقهن

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r5.speaker: أصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r5.claim: Astronomers identify the seven heavens with the spheres of the Moon, Mercury, Venus, Sun, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, in that order.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r5.anchor: وقال أصحاب الهيئة أقربها إلينا كرة القمر ، وفوقها كرة عطارد

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r6.speaker: أصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r6.claim: They infer planetary order from occultations: the lower body blocks the higher; ancient observers saw the Moon occult all six planets, Mercury Venus, and Venus Mars.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r6.anchor: قالوا ولا طريق إلى معرفة هذا الترتيب إلا من وجهين : الأول : الستر وذلك

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r7.speaker: أصحاب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r7.claim: Occultation establishes that the Sun is above the Moon, but cannot place it relative to the other planets because sunlight obscures them.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r7.anchor: هذا الترتيب على هذا الطريق يدل على كون الشمس فوق القمر لانكسافها به ولكن لا يدل

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r8.claim: One observer claimed to see Venus as a spot on the Sun, but Razi calls this weak because others attribute spots to the Sun itself, as the Moon has a blemish.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r8.anchor: أحدهما : ذكر بعضهم أنه رأى الزهرة كشامة في صحيفة الشمس ، وهذا ضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r9.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r9.claim: Most astronomers use parallax: it is perceptible for the Moon, Mercury, and Venus, absent for Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, and very slight for the Sun, placing the Sun between the groups.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r9.anchor: اختلاف المنظر فإنه محسوس للقمر وعطارد والزهرة وغير محسوس للمريخ والمشتري وزحل

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r10.speaker: أبو الريحان
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r10.claim: Abu Rayhan says parallax can be sensed only for the Moon, undermining the proposed ordering proofs and leaving the Sun's position uncertain.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r10.anchor: إلا أن أبا الريحان قال في ( تلخيصه لفصول الفرغاني ) : إن اختلاف المنظر لا يحس إلا في القمر

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r11.speaker: أصحاب الأرصاد وأرباب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r11.claim: Their cosmology posits nine spheres: seven planetary spheres, an eighth carrying the fixed stars, and a ninth outermost sphere making roughly one daily revolution.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r11.anchor: واعلم أن أصحاب الأرصاد وأرباب الهيئة زعموا أن الأفلاك تسعة ، فالسبعة هي هذه التي ذكرناها

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r12.speaker: أصحاب الأرصاد وأرباب الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r12.claim: They infer an eighth sphere because fixed stars move slowly while planetary carriers move rapidly, and they assume stars move only with their spheres.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r12.anchor: وجدنا لهذه الكواكب الثابتة حركات بطيئة وثبت أن الكواكب لا تتحرك إلا بحركة فلكها

RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r13.claim: Razi objects that fixed stars might move by themselves; this possibility is not eliminated without first disproving free choice.
RAZI-FULL:v2p143#2/r13.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يقال الكواكب تتحرك بأنفسها من غير أن تكون مركوزة في جسم آخر

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r1.claim: Even if stars must be carried, they could be fixed in planetary deferents while the planets occupy their own carriers, requiring no eighth sphere.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r1.anchor: سلمنا ذلك لكن لم لا يجوز أن يقال إن هذه الكواكب مركوزة في ممثلات السيارات

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r2.claim: The fixed-star sphere could lie below the Moon: planets occult only stars near the zodiac, while polar stars might occupy a separate sphere below the Moon.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r2.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن يكون ذلك الفلك تحت فلك القمر فيكون تحت كرات السيارات لا فوقها

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r3.claim: Even proving nine spheres would not disprove a tenth; lack of observational evidence for another sphere does not prove it absent.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r3.anchor: هب أنكم أثبتم هذه الأفلاك التسعة فما الذي دلكم على نفي الفلك العاشر

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r4.claim: A reported investigator says he has not established whether the fixed stars occupy one sphere or nested spheres.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r4.anchor: قال بعض المحققين منهم : إنه ما تبين لي إلى الآن أن كرة الثوابت كرة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r5.claim: The inference to one fixed-star sphere assumes their motions are truly equal; tiny differences could escape observation, as in the example of periods differing by one year over 36,000 years.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r5.anchor: ولكن لعلها لا تكون في الحقيقة واحدة ، لأنا لو قدرنا أن واحدا منها يتمم الدورة

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r6.claim: Even genuinely equal stellar speeds would not prove one sphere, since separate spheres can share a rate, as astronomers themselves say of planetary deferents.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r6.anchor: استواء حركات الثوابت في مقادير حركاتها لا يوجب كونها بأسرها مركوزة في كرة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r7.claim: The same uncertainty applies to the daily rotating heaven: it might be several bodies with imperceptibly different motions or distinct bodies with equal motions.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r7.anchor: فلعل الجرم المتحرك بالحركة اليومية ليس جرما واحدا بل أجراما كثيرة إما مختلفة الحركات

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r8.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r8.claim: Some astronomers posit an additional sphere between the fixed stars and the outermost sphere, partly to explain changing measurements of the obliquity of the ecliptic.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r8.anchor: ومن أصحاب الهيئة من قطع بإثبات أفلاك أخر غير هذه التسعة فإن من الناس من أثبت كرة فوق كرة الثوابت

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r9.speaker: أصحاب الأرصاد
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r9.claim: Observers disagreed about the Sun's annual motion; Ptolemy says Hipparchus doubted whether its return took equal or unequal times.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r9.anchor: حتى أن بطليموس حكى عن أبرخيس أنه كان شاكا في أن هذه العودة تكون في أزمنة متساوية

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r10.speaker: أصحاب الرأي الأول
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r10.claim: One explanation makes the Sun's apogee move, changing its distance from the equinox and therefore the time it takes to travel.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r10.anchor: قول من يجعل أوج الشمس متحركا فإنه زعم أن الاختلاف الذي يلحق حركة الشمس من هذه الجهة

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r11.speaker: أهل الهند والصين وبابل وأكثر قدماء الروم ومصر والشام
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r11.claim: Another explanation attributes the variation to movement of the zodiac sphere and changing pole elevation; Hipparchus is said to have held this view.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r11.anchor: قول أهل الهند والصين وبابل وأكثر قدماء الروم ومصر والشام : إن السبب فيه انتقال فلك البروج

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r12.speaker: أصحاب الطلسمات
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r12.claim: Astrologers reportedly believed the zodiac's starting point advances and retreats by eight degrees, beginning at 27 Pisces and returning to Aries' start.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r12.anchor: وذكر بارياء الإسكندراني أن أصحاب الطلسمات كانوا يعتقدون ذلك وأن نقطة فلك البروج تتقدم عن موضعها

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r13.claim: The confusion in astronomical accounts shows human reason cannot master these matters; one should rely on transmitted proofs, and naming seven heavens does not exclude more.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r13.anchor: هذا الخبط مما ينبهك على أنه لا سبيل للعقول البشرية إلى إدراك هذه الأشياء

RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r14.claim: Specifying seven heavens does not imply that no additional heavens exist; mentioning a number does not negate a larger number.
RAZI-FULL:v2p144/r14.anchor: الحق أن تخصيص العدد بالذكر لا يدل على نفي الزائد

RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r1.claim: Creating Earth's and the heavens' wonders requires God to know them, including their particulars and universals.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r1.anchor: لا يمكن أن يكون خالقا للأرض وما فيها وللسموات وما فيها من العجائب والغرائب إلا إذا كان عالما بها

RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r2.claim: The verse refutes philosophers who deny God's knowledge of particulars and supports theologians: a creator who acts with order and precision must know what he creates.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r2.anchor: فساد قول الفلاسفة الذين قالوا إنه لا يعلم الجزئيات وصحة قول المتكلمين

RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r3.claim: Against Mu'tazilites, Razi argues that specifying a created thing's measure requires will, and will requires detailed knowledge; humans therefore do not originate their own acts, whose details they do not know.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r3.anchor: فساد قول المعتزلة وذلك لأنه سبحانه وتعالى بين أن الخالق للشيء على سبيل التقدير والتحديد

RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r4.claim: Mu'tazilites infer that God knows by essence from combining this verse with 12:76; Razi answers that the general verse 12:76 is qualified by the specific 4:166.
RAZI-FULL:v2p146/r4.anchor: خاص والخاص مقدم على العام . والله تعالى أعلم

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r2.claim: God subjected earthly creatures for human benefit: people dwell on earth and under heaven, navigate by stars, and use other creatures; every thing reveals divine power and lordship.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r2.anchor: سخر لهم جميع المخلوقات على معنى حصول انتفاعهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r3.claim: God also paved the way to experiential knowledge and pointed to His favor, teaching high aspiration by reserving people's works and states for Himself; 41:37 forbids bowing to sun or moon.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r3.anchor: ويقال مهد لهم سبيل العرفان ، ونبههم إلى ما خصهم به من الإحسان

QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r4.claim: The created realms were ordered by God's power; God Himself did not settle upon a creature or place, impossible for the One beyond spatial delimitation.
QUSHAYRI:v1p32/r4.anchor: فالأكوان بقدرته استوت ، لا أن الحق سبحانه بذاته - على مخلوق - استوى

STUDYQURAN:2:29/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r1.claim: God created the things on earth for human beings; related passages include 16:5, 16:13, and 26:166.
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r1.anchor: For God’s creation of things for human beings, see also 16:5; 16:13; 26:166.

STUDYQURAN:2:29/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r2.claim: The creation-for-humanity theme connects with God making creation subservient to people in 22:65, 31:20, and 45:13.
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r2.anchor: This idea also relates to God’s making creation subservient to human beings as in 22:65; 31:20; 45:13.

STUDYQURAN:2:29/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r3.claim: Istawā is rendered here as turned to and elsewhere as mounted, including in the cited passages.
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r3.anchor: Turned to translates the verb istawā, which is also rendered “mounted” in other contexts

STUDYQURAN:2:29/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r4.claim: The seven heavens connect to the six-day creation in 41:12, their being one above another in 67:3, and earths like them in 65:12.
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r4.anchor: For the seven heavens, also see 41:12, where the context is the six days of creation; 67:3, in which they are one upon another; 65:12

STUDYQURAN:2:29/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r5.speaker: Mujāhid
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r5.claim: Mujāhid describes the heavens as above one another and the earths as above one another.
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r5.anchor: the early Quran commentator Mujāhid (d. 104/722–23) mentions “heavens above one other” and “earths above one another”

STUDYQURAN:2:29/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r6.claim: Another related passage describes the heavens as having levels.
STUDYQURAN:2:29/r6.anchor: and 71:15, which also mentions the “levels” of heavens.

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.claim: God reminds hypocrites and Jewish scholars of past favors despite their sins, warning of punishment like that of their predecessors while urging repentance for salvation at Judgment; he links their story to the warning at 2:6.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r4.anchor: يحذرهم بذلك تعجيل العقوبة لهم كالتي عجلها للأسلاف والأفراط قبلهم، ويخوفهم حلول مثلاته بساحتهم

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.claim: The following account of Adam shows God's honor to humanity, the consequences of disobedience for Adam and Iblis, mercy for Adam's repentance, and punishment for Iblis's pride and refusal to repent.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r5.anchor: فبدأ بعد تعديده عليهم ما عدد من نعمه التي هم فيها مقيمون بذكر أبينا وأبيهم آدم أبي البشر، صلوات الله عليه، وما سلف منه من كرامته إليه وآلائه لديه

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.claim: These stories address the People of the Book, who know them from their scriptures, and serve as evidence to them that Muhammad is God's messenger: he could not have learned their hidden accounts from books or their community.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r6.anchor: وخاصا أهل الكتاب بما ذكر من قصص آدم وسائر القصص التي ذكرها معها وبعدها مما علمه أهل الكتاب وجهلته الأمة الأمية

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r7.claim: Everything on earth benefits humanity: it provides evidence of God's oneness in religion and livelihood and means in worldly life to obey Him and fulfill obligations.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r7.anchor: لأن الأرض وجميع ما فيها لبني آدم منافع. أما في الدين فدليل على وحدانية ربهم، وأما في الدنيا فمعاش وبلاغ لهم إلى طاعته

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r8.claim: The pronoun 'He' refers back to God's name in the preceding phrase, 'How can you disbelieve in God?'​
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r8.anchor: وقوله: هو مكني من اسم الله جل ذكره، عائد على اسمه في قوله: {كيف تكفرون بالله} [البقرة: 28]

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r9.claim: Here creating means bringing the thing itself out of nonexistence into existence.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r9.anchor: ومعنى خلقه ما خلق جل ثناؤه: إنشاؤه عينه، وإخراجه من حال العدم إلى الوجود.

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r10.claim: The word mā functions as the relative pronoun meaning 'that which.'

TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.claim: God made them living humans after they were semen in their fathers' loins, will kill and raise them for reward or punishment, and provides earthly livelihoods and proofs of His oneness.
TAB-FULL:v1p451/r11.anchor: فمعنى الكلام إذا: كيف تكفرون بالله وقد كنتم نطفا في أصلاب آبائكم، فجعلكم بشرا أحياء، ثم يميتكم

TAB-FULL:v1p454/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p454/r1.claim: Qatada explains that God subjected everything on earth for humanity.
TAB-FULL:v1p454/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: " قوله: {هو الذي خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا} [البقرة: 29] نعم والله سخر لكم ما في الأرض "

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r1.claim: Some interpret istawā ilā as turning toward the heaven, by analogy with Arabic expressions for turning toward or against someone.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r1.anchor: فزعم أنه عنى به أنهن خرجن من الضجوع، وكان ذلك عنده بمعنى أقبلن.

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r2.claim: Tabari rejects the poet's proposed sense of coming toward; he reads the horses as straightening onto the road as they emerged from their bedding.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r2.anchor: وهذا من التأويل في هذا البيت خطأ، وإنما معنى قوله: واستوين من الضجوع عندي: استوين على الطريق

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r3.claim: Some say the phrase does not imply a divine transition; it describes a change in God's action, like a caliph changing his conduct from Iraq to Syria.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لم يكن ذلك من الله جل ذكره بتحول، ولكنه بمعنى فعله، كما تقول: كان الخليفة في أهل العراق

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r4.claim: Some take istawā ilā al-samāʾ to mean that the heaven became level or settled, citing a poet's use of istawā.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: قوله {ثم استوى إلى السماء} [البقرة: 29] يعني به: استوت كما قال الشاعر

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r5.claim: Some say God intended the heaven; anything that leaves one task for another is described as turning toward what it intends.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: {ثم استوى إلى السماء} [البقرة: 29] عمد إليها. وقال: بل كل تارك عملا كان فيه

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r6.claim: Rabīʿ b. Anas glosses the phrase as God rising to the heaven.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r6.anchor: وممن قال ذلك الربيع بن أنس

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r7.claim: Among those who read istiwāʾ as elevation, some identify the one rising above the heaven as its Creator and originator.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r7.anchor: فقال بعضهم: الذي استوى إلى السماء وعلا عليها: هو خالقها ومنشؤها.

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r8.claim: Others say the elevated thing was the smoke God made into the earth's heaven.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم: بل العالي إليها الدخان الذي جعله الله للأرض سماء.

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r9.claim: Tabari says Arabic istiwāʾ can describe a man reaching the full vigor of youth and strength.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r9.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: الاستواء في كلام العرب منصرف على وجوه: منها انتهاء شباب الرجل وقوته، فيقال إذا صار كذلك: قد استوى الرجل

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r10.claim: Another Arabic use is an affair becoming straight after it was crooked; Tabari cites this as a meaning of istawā.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r10.anchor: ومنها استقامة ما كان فيه أود من الأمور والأسباب، يقال منه: استوى لفلان أمره: إذا استقام له بعد أود.

TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r11.claim: Ṭirimmāḥ b. Ḥakīm's poem uses istawā of a place becoming straight or settled.
TAB-FULL:v1p454#2/r11.anchor: طال على رسم مهدد أبده … وعفا واستوى به بلده

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r1.claim: Tabari explains the preceding poetic phrase istawā bihi baladuhu as the place becoming straight, then adds other Arabic meanings of the verb.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r1.anchor: يعني: استقام به. ومنها الإقبال على الشيء بالفعل، كما يقال: استوى فلان على فلان

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r2.claim: Istiwaʾ can mean possessing or taking control, as in taking possession of a kingdom.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r2.anchor: ومنها الاحتياز والاستيلاء كقولهم: استوى فلان على المملكة، بمعنى احتوى عليها وحازها.

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r3.claim: Istiwaʾ also means elevation and height, as when someone is described as elevated above his couch.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r3.anchor: ومنها العلو والارتفاع، كقول القائل: استوى فلان على سريره، يعني به علوه عليه.

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r4.claim: For this verse, Tabari prefers that God rose above the heavens and then ordered them by His power and created them as seven.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r4.anchor: وأولى المعاني بقول الله جل ثناؤه: {ثم استوى إلى السماء فسواهن} [البقرة: 29] علا عليهن وارتفع فدبرهن بقدرته

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r5.claim: Tabari rejects the objection that elevation entails movement: one can affirm elevation as dominion and sovereignty, without transition or displacement; interpreting it as turning toward raises a parallel objection.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r5.anchor: قيل له: فكذلك فقل: علا عليها علو ملك وسلطان لا علو انتقال وزوال.

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r6.claim: God's istiwāʾ occurred after the heaven existed as smoke but before He fashioned it into seven heavens, as 41:11 says.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r6.anchor: والاستواء كان بعد أن خلقها دخانا، وقبل أن يسويها سبع سموات.

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r7.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r7.claim: Some say the heaven was not yet a heaven when God said He turned toward it, comparing the wording to making cloth when only yarn is present.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: إنما قال استوى إلى السماء ولا سماء، كقول الرجل لآخر: اعمل هذا الثوب، وإنما معه غزل.

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r8.claim: Tabari explains fasawwāhunna as preparing, creating, managing, and setting the heavens straight.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r8.anchor: وأما قوله {فسواهن} [البقرة: 29] فإنه يعني هيأهن وخلقهن ودبرهن وقومهن،

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r9.claim: In Arabic, taswiya means straightening, correcting, repairing, or preparing something.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r9.anchor: والتسوية في كلام العرب: التقويم والإصلاح والتوطئة، كما يقال: سوى فلان لفلان هذا الأمر:

TAB-FULL:v1p457/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r10.claim: God ordered the heavens according to His will and managed them according to His purpose, splitting them after they had been joined.
TAB-FULL:v1p457/r10.anchor: تقويمه إياهن على مشيئته، وتدبيره لهن على إرادته، وتفتيقهن بعد ارتتاقهن

TAB-FULL:v1p458/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r1.claim: Rabīʿ b. Anas glosses fasawwāhunna as forming or fashioning the heavens' creation.
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r1.anchor: كما حدثت عن عمار، قال: حدثنا ابن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع بن أنس

TAB-FULL:v1p458/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r2.claim: The verse first treats al-samāʾ as one, then uses the plural feminine pronoun because samāʾ is a collective whose singular is samāwa, like words for cattle and date palms.
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r2.anchor: فأخرجها على تقدير الواحد. وإنما أخرج مكنيهن مخرج مكني الجمع؛ لأن السماء جمع واحدها سماوة

TAB-FULL:v1p458/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r3.claim: One grammarian says al-samāʾ is singular in form but denotes the heavens, so the plural pronoun includes the mentioned heaven and the other heavens it implies.
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r3.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العربية يزعم أن السماء واحدة، غير أنها تدل على السموات، فقيل: {فسواهن}

TAB-FULL:v1p458/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r4.claim: The grammarian notes that al-samāʾ may be grammatically feminine or masculine, citing 73:18 and Arabic poetic examples of feminine forms.
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r4.anchor: وإنما تذكر إذا ذكرت وهي مؤنثة، فيقال: {السماء منفطر به} [المزمل: 18] كما يذكر المؤنث

TAB-FULL:v1p458/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r5.claim: Another view treats heaven as one in meaning but collective in reference, like a garment or pot described by its many worn or broken parts.
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: السماء وإن كانت سماء فوق سماء، وأرضا فوق أرض، فهي في التأويل واحدة

TAB-FULL:v1p458/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r6.claim: Tabari answers that the heavens were already seven, but had not yet been leveled; therefore the verse says He fashioned them as seven.
TAB-FULL:v1p458/r6.anchor: إنهن كن سبعا غير مستويات، فلذلك قال جل ذكره: فسواهن سبعا

TAB-FULL:v1p461/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p461/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v1p461/r1.claim: Ibn Isḥāq narrates that God first made light and darkness, raised seven heavens from smoke, then spread and provisioned the earth, fashioned the heavens, placed the sun, moon, and stars, and completed creation in six days.
TAB-FULL:v1p461/r1.anchor: كما حدثني محمد بن حميد، قال: حدثنا سلمة بن الفضل، قال: قال محمد بن إسحاق:

TAB-FULL:v1p461/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p461/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p461/r2.claim: Tabari uses Ibn Isḥāq's account to argue that the heavens were already seven and smoky before God's fashioning them, and that al-samāʾ here functions collectively.
TAB-FULL:v1p461/r2.anchor: لأنه أوضح بيانا عن خبر السموات أنهن كن سبعا من دخان قبل استواء ربنا إليها

TAB-FULL:v1p463/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p463/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v1p463/r1.claim: Al-Suddī's report from Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and other Companions describes smoke and water becoming the heavens and earth, the earth on a cosmic fish, mountains stabilizing it, provisions and plants, seven heavens, celestial decoration, and six-day completion.
TAB-FULL:v1p463/r1.anchor: عن السدي، في خبر ذكره عن أبي مالك، وعن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس، وعن مرة، عن ابن مسعود

TAB-FULL:v1p464/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r1.claim: Mujāhid says the earth was created before the heaven; smoke rose from the earth, and the seven heavens and seven earths lie one above another and one below another.
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد:

TAB-FULL:v1p464/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r2.claim: Qatāda says the seven heavens are layered one above another, with a journey of five hundred years between each pair.
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r2.anchor: قال: أنبأنا عبد الرزاق، قال: أخبرنا معمر، عن قتادة:

TAB-FULL:v1p464/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reconciles the order by saying earth and its provisions were created before heaven, while the earth was spread out only afterward, as 79:30 states.
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r3.anchor: حدثني معاوية بن صالح، عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس:

TAB-FULL:v1p464/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن سلام
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. Salām says earth was created Sunday and Monday, provisions and mountains Tuesday and Wednesday, and heavens Thursday and Friday; Adam was made in Friday's final hour, the hour of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r4.anchor: قال: حدثني أبو معشر، عن سعيد بن أبي سعيد، عن عبد الله بن سلام:

TAB-FULL:v1p464/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r5.claim: God created and subjected everything on earth for people as a favor, worldly provision, and proof of His oneness, then rose to the smoky heavens, fashioned them, and apportioned their creatures and celestial bodies.
TAB-FULL:v1p464/r5.anchor: فمعنى الكلام إذا: هو الذي أنعم عليكم، فخلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا وسخره لكم تفضلا منه بذلك عليكم

TAB-FULL:v1p465/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r1.claim: Tabari identifies He as God Himself: the Creator knows what hypocrites and scriptural scholars conceal, including false professions of faith, rejection of Muhammad's prophethood, and all other human affairs.
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r1.anchor: ما تبدون وما تكتمون في أنفسكم، وإن أبدى منافقوكم بألسنتهم قولهم: {آمنا بالله وباليوم الآخر}

TAB-FULL:v1p465/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r2.claim: Tabari says ʿalīm means ʿālim, one who knows.
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r2.anchor: وقوله: {عليم} [البقرة: 29] بمعنى عالم. وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقول

TAB-FULL:v1p465/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines the knower as one whose knowledge is complete.
TAB-FULL:v1p465/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: «العالم الذي قد كمل في علمه»

SULAMI:v1p53#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r1.claim: God created earthly things as means to strengthen people in obedience, not to spend them in disobedience.
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r1.anchor: تستعينوا لتقووا به على طاعته لا لتصرفوه في وجوه معصيته

SULAMI:v1p53#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r2.claim: Creation's benefits count God's favors and should prompt gratitude and a request for more.
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : خلق لكم ما في الأرض ليعد نعمه عليكم فيقتضي الشكر من نفسك لطلب المزيد منه

SULAMI:v1p53#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r3.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r3.claim: God gives and subjugates everything as evidence of His generosity, reassurance about the promised afterlife, and a reason not to weigh abundant grace against scant work; gratitude for blessings precedes deeds and is tawhid.
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : وهب لك الكل وسخره لك ؛ لتستدل به على سعة جوده وتسكن إلى ما ضمنه لك

SULAMI:v1p53#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r4.claim: The whole cosmos is for you so that you may belong wholly to God and not be distracted from Him.
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : ﴿ خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ﴾ ليكون الكون كله لك

SULAMI:v1p53#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r5.speaker: بعض البغداديين
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r5.claim: The gifts can overwhelm people into serving blessings; the purified person relinquishes that vision and sees the Benefactor.
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r5.anchor: وقال بعض البغداديين في قوله : ﴿ خلق لكم ما في الأرض جميعا ﴾ أنعم بها عليك

SULAMI:v1p53#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن النوري
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r6.claim: For people at the stations of spiritual realities, the way is to sever attachments.
SULAMI:v1p53#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن النوري : على مقامات أهل الحقائق انقطاعهم عن العلائق

TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.claim: The passage rebukes and reminds people of God's favors: He brings them from death to life, through further death and life to return, and grants creation, the earth, the heavens, succession, angelic honor, the Garden, repentance, worship, and guidance.
TABATABAI:2:28-29/r2.anchor: وفيه ذكر جمل ما خص الله تعالى به الإنسان من مواهب التكوين والتشريع

TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.claim: Humans and other natural beings are formed in relations of acting and being acted upon that sustain existence, but humanity has a broader range of action.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r3.anchor: وكل موجود من الموجودات الطبيعية كذلك، أي إنه مفطور على الارتباط مع غيره ليفعل وينفعل ويستبقي به موهبة وجوده

TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.claim: Human intellect enables complex acts beyond other beings, including composition, destruction, and repair; people imitate or counter nature and benefit from all things, manifesting the subjection of creation to them.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#2/r4.anchor: فهو من جهة تجهيزة بالإدراك والفكر يختص بتصرفات خارجة عن طوق سائر الموجودات بالتفصيل والتركيب والإفساد والإصلاح

TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r1.claim: Because the passage presents blessings to complete God's favor, His directing Himself to heaven and making seven heavens is for humanity; the author invites further reflection.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r1.anchor: وكون الكلام واقعا موقع بيان النعم لتمام الامتنان يعطي أن يكون الاستواء إلى السماء لأجل الإنسان فيكون تسويتها سبعا أيضا لأجله

TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r5.claim: The discussion of the heavens is deferred to the commentary on Sūrat Ḥāʾ Mīm al-Sajdah.
TABATABAI:2:28-29#3/r5.anchor: سيأتي الكلام في السماء في سورة حم السجدة إن شاء الله تعالى

AKHFASH:v1p61/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p61/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p61/r1.claim: The singular السماء signals all the heavens, so the plural pronoun in فسواهن refers to them; the author calls this explanation good.

AKHFASH:v1p61/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p61/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
AKHFASH:v1p61/r2.claim: Some exegetes take السماء as a collective singular, like اللبن, whose meaning is plural; the author rejects this as unattested Arab usage.
AKHFASH:v1p61/r2.anchor: وقد زعم بعض المفسرين ان "السماء" جميع مثل "اللبن"

AKHFASH:v1p61/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p61/r3.speaker: يونس
AKHFASH:v1p61/r3.claim: Yunus says السماء in 65:12 is masculine, as a feminine noun may take masculine agreement; he cites poetry with أبقل and أودى.
AKHFASH:v1p61/r3.anchor: وقال يونس: {السمآء منفطر به} ذكر كما يذكر بعض المؤنث كما قال الشاعر

AKHFASH:v1p61/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p61/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p61/r4.claim: السماء can also refer to a whole class, as in saying the sheep and camel perished to mean every sheep and camel; مثلهن in 2:12 means earths.
AKHFASH:v1p61/r4.anchor: وقد تكون "السماء" يريد به الجماعة كما تقول: "هلك الشاة والبعير" يعني كل بعير وكل شاة

AKHFASH:v1p61/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p61/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p61/r5.claim: God's استواء here does not mean a change of place; it means His action turned toward the heaven, like a caliph whose governing action shifts regions.
AKHFASH:v1p61/r5.anchor: فان ذلك لم يكن من الله تبارك وتعالى

TABRISI:2:29/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r1.claim: خلق means measuring or determining; الجمع means joining and is opposed to separating.
TABRISI:2:29/r1.anchor: أصل الخلق التقدير والجمع الضم ونقيضه الفرق

TABRISI:2:29/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r2.claim: استواء means upright balance or straightness, opposed to crookedness.

TABRISI:2:29/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r3.claim: سبع is feminine and سبعة masculine; seven suggests multiplied strength, as if increased sevenfold.
TABRISI:2:29/r3.anchor: والسبع للمؤنث والسبعة للمذكر والسبع مشتق من ذلك لأنه مضاعف القوى

TABRISI:2:29/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:29/r4.claim: Al-ʿAlim means “knowing”; Sibawayh says فعيل is an intensive form, as in عليم and رحيم.
TABRISI:2:29/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه إذا أرادوا المبالغة عدوا إلى فعيل نحو عليم ورحيم

TABRISI:2:29/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r5.speaker: المفسرون
TABRISI:2:29/r5.claim: Commentators say God recalls creating the heavens and earth to answer polytheists who found resurrection implausible, showing His power to recreate.
TABRISI:2:29/r5.anchor: قال المفسرون لما استعظم المشركون أمر الإعادة عرفهم الله تعالى خلق السموات والأرض ليدلهم بذلك على قدرته

TABRISI:2:29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r6.claim: Everything on earth is made for people: religious benefits let them infer God, while worldly benefits serve them in many ways.
TABRISI:2:29/r6.anchor: ومعناه أن الأرض وجميع ما فيها نعم من الله تعالى مخلوقة لكم إما دينية فتستدلون بها على معرفته

TABRISI:2:29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r7.claim: One explanation is that God directed Himself to heaven to arrange it, like a ruler shifting from governing Syria to the Hejaz.
TABRISI:2:29/r7.anchor: أحدها: أن معناه قصد السماء ولتسويتها كقول القائل كان الأمير يدير أمر الشام ثم استوى إلى أهل الحجاز

TABRISI:2:29/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r8.claim: Another explanation is mastery by power and unique sovereignty over heaven; لتستووا على ظهوره and poetry support استوى as mastery.
TABRISI:2:29/r8.anchor: وثانيها: أنه بمعنى استولى على السماء بالقهر كما قال لتستووا على ظهوره أي تقهروه

TABRISI:2:29/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r9.claim: This explanation uses استوى for becoming established in one's affair, as in 28:14, and cites poetry for mastery.
TABRISI:2:29/r9.anchor: أي تمكن من أمره وقهر هواه بعقله

TABRISI:2:29/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:29/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says God's command and decrees ascended to heaven, from which they descend to earth.
TABRISI:2:29/r10.anchor: ثم استوى أمره وصعد إلى السماء لأن أوامره وقضاياه تنزل من السماء إلى الأرض عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:29/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r11.speaker: ثعلب أحمد بن يحيى
TABRISI:2:29/r11.claim: Thaʿlab, Ahmad ibn Yahya, explains استوى as turning or attending to something, as when someone turns to another to speak.
TABRISI:2:29/r11.anchor: ثعلب أحمد بن يحيى أنه سئل عن معنى الاستواء

TABRISI:2:29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r12.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to السماء because that word is a collective genus for few and many.
TABRISI:2:29/r12.anchor: فجمع الضمير العائد إلى السماء لأن السماء اسم جنس يدل على القليل والكثير

TABRISI:2:29/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r13.claim: Another account derives السماء from the collective سماوة or سماءة, explaining why it may be feminine or masculine.
TABRISI:2:29/r13.anchor: وقيل السماء جمع سماوة وسماءة ولذلك يؤنث مرة ويذكر أخرى

TABRISI:2:29/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r14.claim: The skies may be conceived as one layered heaven but described as seven regions, like collective expressions for things divided into parts.
TABRISI:2:29/r14.anchor: وقيل إن السماوات كانت سماء فوق سماء فهي في التقدير واحدة وتكون الواحدة جماعة

TABRISI:2:29/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29/r15.claim: God made the seven heavens level and sound, without fissures or defects.
TABRISI:2:29/r15.anchor: جعلهن سبع سموات مستويات بلا فطور ولا أمت

TABRISI:2:29/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29/r16.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:2:29/r16.claim: Ali ibn Isa says the heavens differ from the moving, revolving celestial spheres, citing 35:41.
TABRISI:2:29/r16.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: إن السموات غير الأفلاك لأن الأفلاك تتحرك

TABRISI:2:29#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29#2/r1.claim: The author calls Ali ibn Isa's distinction weak: 35:41 means the spheres stay in their centers because God sustains them, not that they do not move.
TABRISI:2:29#2/r1.anchor: وهذا قول ضعيف لأن قوله أن تزولا معناه لا تزول عن مراكزها التي تدور عليها

TABRISI:2:29#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29#2/r2.speaker: الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد
TABRISI:2:29#2/r2.claim: To reconcile earth's creation before heaven with its spreading afterward in 79:30, they say God created it first but spread it after creating heaven.
TABRISI:2:29#2/r2.anchor: دحوها بسطها ومدها عن الحسن وعمرو بن عبيد

TABRISI:2:29#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29#2/r3.claim: Alternatively, ثم and بعد may order the blessings being recounted, not the timing of creation; verbal order need not equal event order.
TABRISI:2:29#2/r3.anchor: وقد يجوز أيضا أن لا يكون معنى ثم وبعد في هذه الآيات الترتيب في الأوقات وإنما هو على جهة تعداد النعم

TABRISI:2:29#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29#2/r4.claim: After power and sovereignty, the verse names knowledge because power and knowledge together produce precise, well-ordered action.
TABRISI:2:29#2/r4.anchor: لما وصف نفسه بالقدرة والاستيلاء وصل ذلك بالعلم إذ بهما يصح وقوع الفعل على وجه الاتقان والإحكام

TABRISI:2:29#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29#2/r5.claim: God's knowledge of people's outcomes and the outcome of His gifts makes those gifts true blessings.
TABRISI:2:29#2/r5.anchor: عالم بما يؤول إليه حاله وحال المنعم به عليه فتتحقق بذلك النعمة

TABRISI:2:29#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29#2/r6.claim: The verse shows the creator is powerful and knowing, acts for a purpose, and has given disbelievers blessings that require gratitude.
TABRISI:2:29#2/r6.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن صانع السماء والأرض قادر وعالم وأنه تعالى إنما يفعل الفعل لغرض

TABRISI:2:29#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:29#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:29#2/r7.claim: The default rule for things is permissibility: God made earthly things for human benefit, while exclusive control of any thing requires evidence.
TABRISI:2:29#2/r7.anchor: وفيها أيضا دلالة على أن الأصل في الأشياء الإباحة لأنه ذكر أنه خلق ما في الأرض لمنفعة العباد

FARRA:v1p24/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p24/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p24/r7.claim: Arabic uses استوى for reaching maturity and for becoming straight after crookedness.
FARRA:v1p24/r7.anchor: الاستواء في كلام العرب على جهتين: إحداهما أن يستوي الرجل

FARRA:v1p24/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p24/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p24/r8.claim: A third Arabic use of استوى is turning or directing oneself toward someone; al-Farrāʾ takes the verse to mean God turned toward heaven.
FARRA:v1p24/r8.anchor: ووجه ثالث أن تقول: كان مقبلا على فلان ثم استوى على يشاتمني

FARRA:v1p24/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p24/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
FARRA:v1p24/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses استوى as “ascended”; al-Farrāʾ says this and the use for changing posture are all valid in Arabic.
FARRA:v1p24/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ثم استوى إلى السماء: صعد،

FARRA:v1p24/r10.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p24/r10.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p24/r10.claim: The singular السماء can denote the collective of seven heavens, which explains the plural pronoun هن in فسواهن.
FARRA:v1p24/r10.anchor: فإن السماء في معنى جمع، فقال «فسواهن» للمعنى المعروف

FARRA:v1p24/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p24/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p24/r11.claim: Arabic may use singular الأرض for a collective and dual reference for grouped heaven and earth; the text says “between them,” not “between them” in feminine plural.
FARRA:v1p24/r11.anchor: وكذلك الأرض يقع عليها- وهى واحدة- الجمع. ويقع عليهما التوحيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r1.claim: Because the polytheists found resurrection extraordinary, God recalls creating the heavens and earth: raising people after first creating them is no more difficult than creating the heavens, earth, and all within them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون لما استعظم المشركون أمر الإعادة عرفهم خلق السموات والأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r2.claim: Here ‘for you’ means ‘for your sake’: earthly things were made for human benefit or as objects of reflection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {لكم} أي: لأجلكم، فما في الأرض مخلوق لهم بعضها للانتفاع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r3.claim: Even harmful beasts, scorpions, and snakes benefit accountable people as lessons and warnings; seeing a sample of threatened punishment more effectively deters sin and encourages obedience, while a sample of promised reward increases longing, since direct sight affects the heart more than report.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p294/r3.anchor: فإن السباع والعقارب والحيات، وكل ما يؤذي ويضر فيها منفعة للمكلفين وجهة ما فيها من العبرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r1.claim: Al-Farra gives ‘istawa’ three Arabic uses: reaching maturity and strength, becoming straight after crookedness, and turning or coming toward someone; the last sense explains the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r1.anchor: عن الفراء قال: (الاستواء) في كلام العرب على جهتين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r2.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r2.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya says istiwaʾ as an attribute of God means turning toward or attending to something.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r2.anchor: سئل أحمد بن يحيى عن (الاستواء) في صفة الله، فقال: الاستواء الإقبال على الشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports interpreters who take istawa as intending or aiming at heaven, like a ruler finishing one country’s affairs and then turning to another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r3.anchor: قال قوم في قوله: {ثم استوى إلى السماء}: عمد وقصد إلى السماء، كما تقول: فرغ الأمير من بلد كذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj cites Ibn Abbas’s ‘ascended to heaven’ and explains it as God’s command ascending to heaven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r4.anchor: وقول ابن عباس: {استوى إلى السماء} أي صعد، معناه صعد أمره إلى السماء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r5.claim: Arabic speakers say a ruler who managed Syria and then ‘istawa to’ the Hijaz has shifted his activity and administration there.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r5.anchor: وحكى أهل اللغة أن العرب تقول: كان الأمير يدبر أهل الشام ثم استوى إلى أهل الحجاز

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r6.claim: Istiwaʾ fundamentally means straightness; intent came to be called istiwaʾ, and vice versa, because the terms overlap in usage, though language itself is not rationalized this way.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r7.claim: Some scholars of meaning explain the naming of intent as istiwaʾ by the terms’ occasional shared use, while acknowledging that language is not explained by rational derivation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r7.anchor: لتسميتهم القصد: استواء وإن كانت اللغة لا تعلل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p295/r8.claim: Istiwaʾ can also mean istawla, ‘took control’: matters became settled for someone, so he gained mastery; istawa then stands in place of istawla.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r1.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash says istawa means rose or was above, as when one rises above a mount or a rooftop.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r2.speaker: محمد بن جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Jarir chooses ‘rose in dominion and authority,’ not physical movement or displacement; the elevation is of governance, judgment, and sovereignty, close to Ibn Abbas and al-Zajjaj’s explanation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r2.anchor: وهذا القول اختيار محمد بن جرير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r3.claim: Taswiya means making things equal or straight; unlike taqwim, it can be an assessment by judgment that two things are equal, whereas taqwim occurs only through action.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r3.anchor: حقيقة (التسوية) الجعل على الاستواء، يقال سويت الشيئين فاستويا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r4.claim: The feminine plural pronoun refers to all the heavens although the word heaven is singular, as a singular may convey a collective; examples include 26:77 and 26:16.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r4.anchor: في {فسواهن} لأنه أراد بلفظ (السماء) جميع السموات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r5.speaker: قطرب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r5.claim: Qutrub’s poetic line is cited as evidence for singular wording used with a collective sense.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r5.anchor: قطرب: ألا إن جيراني العشية رائح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r6.claim: Another possibility is that al-samaʾ is a collective plural of samāh or samāwah, as explained earlier.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالسماء جمع سماة أو سماوة، على ما ذكرنا قبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r7.claim: The feminine plural pronoun may instead refer to the parts or regions of the heaven.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r7.anchor: وجائز أن تعود الكناية على أجزاء السماء ونواحيها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p298/r8.claim: Sabʿ is the feminine form used with a feminine counted noun, while sabʿa is masculine; the author explains their forms as originating before numbers were attached to counted nouns, then being assigned in order to the two genders.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r1.speaker: author
