WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r1.claim: God knows their disbelief and hypocrisy and their concealment of the Prophet’s description.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r1.anchor: أي من كفرهم ونفاقهم وكتمهم وصفك يا محمد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r2.claim: One explanation says knowledge follows the mention of power and dominion because knowledge is necessary for precise, perfected action.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r2.anchor: وقيل: إنه لما ذكر ما يدل على القدرة والاستيلاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r3.claim: Another explanation is that God knows everything involved in creation and fashioning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r3.anchor: بكل شي عليم من الخلق والتسوية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r4.claim: The verse does not say heaven was created after earth; it says heaven was made into seven after earth was created. Exegetes say heaven had already existed as smoke.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r4.anchor: والآية لا تدل على أنه خلق السماء بعد الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r5.claim: Abu Amr and al-Kisaʾi lighten the hāʾ in huwa after waw, fa, and lām, treating these one-letter particles as attached to the word; they do not lighten it after thumma.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r5.anchor: وكان أبو عمرو والكسائي يخففان (وهو)، (فهو) ويسكنان (الهاء) مع الواو والفاء واللام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r6.claim: The reading treats waw, fa, and lām as closely attached because they have no meaning alone; the hāʾ is lightened like medial consonants in sabʿ and ʿuḍud. Thumma is kept separate because it can stand alone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r6.anchor: يجعلان هذه الحروف كأنها من نفس الكلمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r7.claim: The author explains the lightening with examples including the reading wayakhsha Allāha wayattaqihi (24:52), where taqihi is also lightened like katif.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r8.speaker: الخليل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r8.claim: Al-Khalil’s line is cited for lightening a form like yalid to yild as in katif, then restoring a vowel to avoid two adjacent vowelless consonants.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r9.claim: Those who also lighten thumma huwa can argue that thumma, like fa and waw, is external to the word; detached words sometimes assimilate like connected forms, as in yad Dawud and jaʿal lak.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v2p301/r9.anchor: أن يقول (¬6): إن (ثم) مثل الفاء والواو واللام

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r1.claim: Istawā ilā means that God turned or directed Himself toward the heaven.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r1.anchor: ثم استوى إلى السماء} عمد لها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r2.claim: In Arabic usage, one who leaves a task and turns to another has istawā lahu or istawā ilayhi, whether the first task was finished or not.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r2.anchor: وكل من كان يعمل عملا فتركه بفراغ أو غير فراغ وعمد لغيره، فقد استوى له واستوى إليه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p45/r3.claim: The pronoun in fasawwāhunna refers to the seven heavens.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r1.claim: God created everything on earth for people: some things are for use and others for reflection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r1.anchor: ما في الأرض جميعا } بعضها للانتفاع، وبعضها للاعتبار

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r2.claim: Here istawā ilā means that God turned toward creating heaven and directed Himself to it.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r3.claim: He made the seven heavens even and well-proportioned, without fissures, cracks, or disparity.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r3.anchor: فجعلهن سبع سموات مستويات لا شقوق فيها ولا فطور ولا تفاوت

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:29/r4.claim: God’s knowledge makes the perfectly ordered act possible.

ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.claim: Elmalılı says these verses contain the sciences of this world and the hereafter, showing life, its course, and its purpose, as well as the value of human creation before God.
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r1.anchor: Bu iki âyette bütün dünya ve âhiret ilimleri mündericdir. Hayat, cereyân-ı hayât, gāye-i hayât gösteriliyor

ELMALILI:2:28-29/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r2.claim: The verses affirm humanity’s right to benefit from the earth and heavens and summarize the signs of creation and the Creator, establishing God’s creative act, mercy, and favor.
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r2.anchor: İnsanın arz u semâ hepsinden hakk-ı

ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.claim: The passage raises the human spirit from the material and perceptible toward the intelligible, and asks how anyone could turn to disbelief and ingratitude in light of these truths.
ELMALILI:2:28-29/r3.anchor: ve bu hakāik karşısında küfür ve küfrâna nasıl

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r1.claim: God created everything on earth for human use in life and death, to enable human creation and a happy life, and made it available to people.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r1.anchor: Hep bunları insanı yaratmak ve yarattıktan sonra mes‘ud yaşatmak için yarattı

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r2.claim: The general benefit of earthly things does not mean each benefits every person in every way; some can also be harmful.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r2.anchor: bir kısmında mazarrat haysiyeti de vardır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r3.claim: The verse grounds the legal presumption of original permissibility: things are usable unless a specific proof establishes prohibition.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r3.anchor: Nüfûs ve ırz u nâmustan mâ‘adâ eşyâda asl olan ibâhadır. Husûsî bir delîl-i hurmet bulunmadıkça ibâha ile amel olunur

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r4.claim: Original permissibility rests on this revealed text, not reason alone; reason by itself leads people to conflicting judgments about what is permitted.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r4.anchor: Bu ibâhanın delili yalnız akıl değil bu nastır.

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r5.claim: The permission is granted equally to humanity; people were not created for one another, so one person's life and honor are not another's to use.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r5.anchor: bu ibâha insanların umûmuna ‘ale’s-seviyye yapılmış, insanlar insan için yaratılmamış ve yekdiğerine ibâha edilmemiştir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r6.claim: A person cannot dispose of their own life or honor at will, including through suicide or selling themselves; only marriage permitted by God is authorized.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r6.anchor: bir insan kendi canında, ırzında bile dilediği gibi tasarrufa me’zun değildir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r7.claim: A person's actions, wealth, and property are protected from others, but may be given or transferred with the owner's consent; contracts and financial dealings rest on this basis.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r7.anchor: Lâkin kendileri için mubah olduğundan rızâlarıyla diğerlerine de terk ve i‘tâ edebilirler

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r8.claim: Life, liberty, honor, intellect, and religion are fundamental rights belonging directly to God; violating them is a major sin, and their default status is inviolability.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r8.anchor: hakkullah olan hukūk-ı esâsiyesindendir ve bunlara taarruz kebâirdendir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r9.claim: Human beings were created for worship, not merely for self-directed enjoyment of earthly goods.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r9.anchor: insanlar kendileri için değil Allah’a ubudiyet için yaratılmışlardır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r10.claim: After preparing the earth for people, God directed His will to heaven, ordered its parts and especially the seven heavens, and thereby supplied further benefits to earth and humanity.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r10.anchor: semâya doğrulmuş, iradesini göklere tevcih etmiş

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r11.claim: He reads “seven heavens” as a partitive apposition to the plural pronoun: the plural form, rather than a singular pronoun, signals parts, individuals, or kinds.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r11.anchor: فَسَوَّىٰهُنَّ,”سَبْعَ سَمَٰوَٰتٍۢ’den bedeldir. Ve bedel-i ba‘z zâhirdir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.claim: The passage summarizes humanity's pre-life nonexistence, expands the earlier description of earth and heaven as habitation, proves God's lordship, and summons deniers to gratitude and worship.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r12.anchor: nihâyet inâyet ve rahmet-i ilâhiyenin vüs‘ati ile zât ve sıfât-ı ilâhiyeyi münkirlere isbat

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r13.speaker: Şeyh Sa‘dî
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r13.claim: Saadi's poem depicts cloud, wind, moon, sun, and sky as serving people so they can obtain their daily bread, expressing the passage's theme of creation serving human benefit.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r13.anchor: Şeyh Sa‘dî merhum Gülistân’ında bu mazmunu şöyle ifade etmiştir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r14.claim: Humans are not merely earthly creatures: they have a share in heavenly benefits, but spiritual ascent requires sensing their celestial vocation and knowing God; those sunk in sensual life miss it.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#3/r14.anchor: insan yalnız arzî bir mahluk değildir. O yerlerde daralırsa göklerden intifâ‘a mezundur

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r1.claim: The sequence marked by thumma can be rhetorical or rank-based rather than chronological: the account follows human cognition, which begins with the self, then earth, then heaven.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r1.anchor: sonralık, yani ثُمَّ mânası zamânen değil rütbeten, yani ifade nokta-i nazarından bir sonralıktır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r2.claim: People first know earth through touch and bodily weight, then heaven; God speaks in that order, so the verse's surface order alone does not prove earth was created first.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r2.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak da irşâdâtını, idrâk-i beşerin bu cereyânına göre beyan buyurmuştur ki bunu zâhirinden arz semâdan evvel yaratılmış gibi anlamamalıdır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r3.claim: He allows a literal temporal reading too: although earth was not absolutely created before heaven, the formation of earth as a distinct body could follow earlier heavenly ordering, as 21:30 indicates.

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r4.claim: On a physical account, earth's formation and gravity altered the arrangement of its celestial system, so the seven heavens related to earth would have been ordered afterward; unaffected regions lie beyond them.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r4.anchor: câzibe-i arziyye ile alâkadar olan seb‘a semâvât tesviyesi ve nizâm-ı hilkati arzdan evvel değil, sonra olmak lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r5.claim: One astronomy-based proposal counts seven heavens outward from earth through the planetary intervals to beyond Saturn, including Uranus, Neptune, and any planets later discovered within the seventh boundary.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r5.anchor: Arz’dan Zühre’ye kadar bir, Zühre’den Utarid’e iki, Utarid’den Şems’e üç, Şems’ten Mirrih’e yahut yine Arz’dan Mirrih’e dört

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r6.claim: This model is relational to earth and need not imply that earth is the solar system's center; an observer on the sun would count the planetary intervals from there instead.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r6.anchor: bunda mevzû‘-i bahis arzın merkeziyeti değil arza nazaran “semâ” kelimesinin tatbîkidir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r7.speaker: Batlamyus ilm-i hey’etini tâkip edenler
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r7.claim: Ptolemaic astronomers counted the Moon as the first planet and Saturn as the seventh, then tried to fit the Qur'anic heavens to that model.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r7.anchor: Batlamyus hey’etini tâkip edenler Kamer’i birinci seyyare saydıklarından ondan başlarlardı ve yedincisi Zuhal’e dayanırdı

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r8.speaker: Batlamyus ilm-i hey’eti
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r8.claim: Ptolemy's theory assigned each of seven planets a sphere, another sphere to the fixed stars, and an encompassing Atlas sphere whose motion produced daily motion; planetary motion was explained as natural and forced components.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r8.anchor: Seyyârelerde iki hareket görülüyor, bunun biri tabîî ise diğeri her hâlde kasrî olmak lâzım gelir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r9.speaker: ulemâ-yı tefsîr ve mütekellimîn
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r9.claim: Exegetes and theologians argued that Ptolemy's cosmological theory was not certain and that another cause could explain the motions.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r9.anchor: ulemâ-yı tefsîr ve hatta mütekellimîn de bu nazariyenin yakīnî olmadığını, diğer bir sebebin melhuz olabileceğini söylüyorlardı

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r10.speaker: Sâbit b. Kurre
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r10.claim: The philosopher Sābit ibn Qurra had already proposed an attraction theory as an alternative explanation.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r10.anchor: Sâbit b. Kurre bir cezb nazariyesini bile dermeyan etmişti

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r11.claim: Modern astronomy has narrowed its serious work to the solar system, so proposals beyond it remain hypothetical; gravitational theory had no known empirical or inductive counterexample and fits Qur'anic descriptions of unsupported heavens.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r11.anchor: Câzibe-i umûmiye kanunu bugün âdetâ müte‘ârife tavrını almış bir mevzû‘a-i ilmiye olmuştur

ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r12.claim: Because gravity is an abstract, almost spiritual concept, he says it would be more serious and wise to conceive it through an angel and connect it directly to divine power.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#4/r12.anchor: bunu bir “melek” kelimesiyle tasavvur etmek ve bizzat kudret-i ilâhiyeye rabt eylemek daha ciddî ve daha hikemî olurdu

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r1.speaker: ekâbir-i müfessirîn
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r1.claim: Another view makes the star-adorned material cosmos above earth the lowest heaven, with six further heavens beyond it; Elmalılı identifies this as the view of leading exegetes.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r1.anchor: Arz’ın üstünde bütün yıldızların tezyin ettiği maddî âlemin hepsi bir semâdır. Seb‘a semâvâtın birincisidir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r2.claim: If the other heavens are understood as spiritual and intelligible, their correspondence is clearer than a material picture of layered physical space; 37:6 describes the lowest heaven's stars.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r2.anchor: Bunlar rûhânî ve ma‘kul olarak tasavvur edildikleri zaman fezânın ecsâma intibâkı gibi aralarında tıbâk u mutabakat mefhûmu daha bârizdir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r3.claim: Reports of the Prophet's ascension also point to spiritual meanings of the heavens.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r3.anchor: Sonra miraç hadislerinde de semâvâtın böyle rûhânî mânalarına işaret vardır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r4.claim: God continually orders the heavens' varied affairs; this ordering is not limited to matter, and after creating earth He specially ordered them and set angels and effects to prepare the world for people.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r4.anchor: Cenâb-ı Hak her an bunların şu‘ûn-ı muhtelifesini tesviye etmektedir. Ve bu tesviye maddiyâta münhasır değildir

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r5.claim: God's eternal knowledge answers doubts that cosmic events are blind chance or that earth and heaven could have been prepared for life in advance; knowledge underlies sciences and the connection of causes and effects.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r5.anchor: Esbâb ve müsebbebât birbirine nasıl merbut olurdu? Fünun nasıl teessüs ederdi?

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r6.claim: Humanity is the product and small copy, perhaps even the great copy, of earth and heaven, created through divine knowledge, power, and encompassing mercy with its means of happiness prepared.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r6.anchor: insanları böyle yüksek bir ilm ü kudretle, böyle şâmil bir rahmetle arz u semânın bir hâsılası, bir nüsha-i suğrâsı ve belki kübrâsı olarak yaratmıştır

ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.claim: People should recall these gifts, investigate what was prepared for their benefit, use it in God's way, prepare for the afterlife, and aspire upward because they will return to God.
ELMALILI:2:28-29#5/r7.anchor: bu edvârı, bu nimetleri derhâtır ediniz, rûhunuzun ne gibi ulviyetlere namzet kılındığını düşününüz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r1.claim: Scientific disciplines including mathematics, astronomy, and solar physics establish that the earth and heavens had a beginning and did not exist before it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r1.anchor: Yerin ve göklerin bir başlangıcının bulunduğu, bundan önce yer ve göklerin mevcut olmadığı matematik, astronomi, güneş fiziği gibi ilgili bilim dallarınca da tesbit edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r2.speaker: Taşkın Tuna
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r2.claim: The cited account describes a primordial mass of bare atoms expanding explosively into the universe, followed by the formation of atoms, elements, stars, suns, and galaxies; how the first matter arose remains unknown.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r2.anchor: Proton, nötron ve elektronlardan ağır elementler husule geldi. Yıldızlar doğdu, güneşler ortaya çıktı, galaksiler meydana geldi” (Taşkın Tuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r3.speaker: Bilim adamları
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r3.claim: Scientists place the Big Bang billions of years in the past, with the creation of the Milky Way and countless other galaxies beginning billions of years ago and none existing earlier.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r3.anchor: Bilim adamları bu büyük patlamanın tarihini milyarlarca yıl geriye götürmektedirler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r4.claim: Science does not know how the first matter came to exist.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r4.anchor: İlk evren maddesinin nasıl var olduğu bilimin meçhulüdür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r5.speaker: semavî dinler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r5.claim: The revealed religions agree that a creator originated the universe and its subsequent development, endowed with limitless knowledge, wisdom, power, and artistry.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r5.anchor: Bütün semavî dinler bunun bir yaratıcısının olduğu, sonraki gelişmeleri de ilmi sonsuz, hikmeti, kudreti ve sanatı eşsiz olan yaratıcının sağladığı konusunda ittifak etmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r6.claim: The verse says Allah created the earth and also created and ordered the seven heavens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r6.anchor: Bu ve başka âyetlerde yerküreyi Allah yarattığı gibi âyette “yedi sema” diye anılan gökleri de yedi gök olarak yaratıp düzenleyenin Allah olduğu bildirilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r7.speaker: tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r7.claim: Commentators who take the seven heavens as the earth's skies or the skies of space explained them through successive cosmological models, from Aristotle and Ptolemy to Copernicus, Galileo, Kepler, Newton, Einstein, and Hawking.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r7.anchor: Bu yedi göğü dünyanın gökleri veya uzayın gökleri olarak kabul eden tefsirciler, eski Aristo ve Batlamyus nazariyesine göre

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r8.claim: The exact referent of the seven heavens is not known with certainty.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r8.anchor: Ancak bu yedi gökten maksadın ne olduğu konusunda kesin bir bilgi yoktur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r9.claim: In Arabic usage, seven may function as a figure for multitude, so the phrase can mean many heavens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r9.anchor: Arap dilindeki kullanıma göre bunun çokluktan kinaye olarak düşünülüp birçok gök şeklinde anlaşılması da mümkündür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r10.speaker: tasavvuf ve irfan kolu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r10.claim: The author introduces alternative and intriguing explanations of the seven heavens from the Sufi and mystical tradition enriched by unveiling and inspiration.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r10.anchor: Öte yandan, keşif ve ilham kaynağı ile zenginleştirilmiş bulunan tasavvuf ve irfan kolunda, “yedi gök”le ilgili farklı ve ilgi çekici açıklamalar vardır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r11.claim: One mystical account divides all that Allah created into the material, corporeal world of creation and the incorporeal, subtle world of command, separated by the Throne.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r11.anchor: Halk âlemi maddîdir, cisimlidir; emir âlemi cisimsizdir, latiftir. Bu iki âlemi birbirinden “arş” ayırır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r12.claim: In this account materiality thins upward toward immateriality; the vast but comparatively small material universe is the lowest layer and is not included among the seven heavens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r12.anchor: Halk âleminin en alt katında, bütün büyüklük ve sonsuzluk görüntüsü içinde, bir yukarısına göre çok küçük olan evren vardır. Bu evren maddîdir. Kur’an’da geçen yedi semaya dahil değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r13.claim: The first heaven above the universe is compared in scale to a sea beside a drop, and the same proportional expansion continues upward through the heavens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r13.anchor: bu semanın –bütün galaksileriyle birlikte– evrenden büyüklüğü, damlaya nisbetle deniz gibidir. Bu oran yukarıya doğru aynı ölçülerde büyüyerek devam eder.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r14.claim: Above the seventh heaven are the Kursi and then the Throne; beyond the Throne begins the world of command, containing subtle centers that constitute human spiritual reality, each higher one encompassing the lower.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r14.anchor: Yedinci semadan sonra kürsî, ondan sonra da arş vardır. Arşın üstünden itibaren emir âlemi başlar. Burada insanın hakikatini ve mânevî mahiyetini teşkil eden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r15.claim: The spiritual centers are called heart, spirit, secret, hidden, and most hidden; the hadith about the believer's vast heart refers to the subtle heart.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r15.anchor: Bazı hadislerde geçen ve çok geniş olduğundan söz edilen “mümin kalbi” işte bu latîfe olan kalptir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r16.speaker: hadisler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r16.claim: Mi'raj and other hadiths mention spirits, angels, paradises, and other beings located in these heavens.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r16.anchor: Bu semalarda ruhlar, melekler, cennetler vb. varlıkların yer aldığı, mi‘rac hadisi vb. hadislerde geçmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r17.claim: All these created realities are made by God, who knows and can do all things, and they act only within His permission and will.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r17.anchor: Bütün bunlar, her şeyi hakkıyla bilen ve her şeye kadir olan Allah Teâlâ tarafından yaratılmıştır, O’nun izni ve iradesi dahilinde hareket ederler.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r18.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r18.claim: The commentary points readers to Qur'an 7:54 for the meanings and explanation of the terms creation and command.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:29/r18.anchor: anlamları ve açıklaması için bk. A’râf 7/54

NAHHAS:v1p206/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r1.claim: The clause begins with a subject and predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r1.anchor: ابتداء وخبر ( ما ) في موضع نصب

NAHHAS:v1p206/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r3.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v1p206/r3.claim: Sībawayh parses «جميعا» as an accusative circumstantial.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r3.anchor: ( جميعا ) عند سيبويه نصب على الحال

NAHHAS:v1p206/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r4.claim: The people of the Hijaz pronounce the alif with tafkhīm, while Najd speakers use imāla to indicate its origin in yāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r4.anchor: أهل الحجاز يفخمون وأهل نجد يميلون ليدلوا على أنه من ذوات الياء

NAHHAS:v1p206/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r6.speaker: محمد بن الوليد
NAHHAS:v1p206/r6.claim: Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd parses «سبع» as an accusative apposition to the object pronoun «هن».
NAHHAS:v1p206/r6.anchor: قال محمد بن الوليد سبع منصوب على أنه بدل من الهاء والنون

NAHHAS:v1p206/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar allows an implied partitive «منهن», as in «اختار موسى قومه» meaning he chose from his people.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r7.anchor: قال أبو جعفر يجوز عندي أن يكون فسوى منهن كما قال جل وعز واختار موسى قومه

NAHHAS:v1p206/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p206/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p206/r8.claim: The clause is nominal, with a subject and predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p206/r8.anchor: ( وهو بكل شيء عليم ) مبتدأ وخبر

BURHAN:v1p90/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p90/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p90/r6.claim: These subtle verse endings seem at first to call for the reverse attributes, but close consideration shows the transmitted endings are fitting as recited.
BURHAN:v1p90/r6.anchor: فإن المتبادر إلى الذهن فى آية البقرة الختم بالقدرة وفى آية آل عمران الختم بالعلم

BURHAN:v2p77/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p77/r7.speaker: سفيان الثوري
BURHAN:v2p77/r7.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says he understands the phrase as he understands ثم استوى إلى السماء, comparing the two expressions.
BURHAN:v2p77/r7.anchor: وكذلك سئل سفيان الثوري فقال أفهم من قوله ﴿ الرحمن على العرش استوى ﴾ 1 ما أفهم من قوله ﴿ ثم استوى إلى السماء ﴾

BURHAN:v2p62/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p62/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p62/r3.claim: There is no conflict: earth and its contents were created before the heavens, then earth was spread out after the heavens, harmonizing the cited passages.
BURHAN:v2p62/r3.anchor: ولا تنافي بينهما فالأول ( 8 ) دال على أن الأرض وما فيها خلقت ( 9 ) قبل السماء

ITQAN:v3p275/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p275/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p275/r4.claim: The creation of the earth and its benefits, and the heavens’ ordered construction, make “Knowing all things” an apt ending: a creator of this kind must know His work in every detail.
ITQAN:v3p275/r4.anchor: والجواب أن آية البقرة لما تضمنت الإخبار عن خلق الأرض وما فيها على حسب حاجات أهلها ومنافعهم ومصالحهم وخلق السموات خلقا مستويا محكما من غير تفاوت

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f5.claim: The preceding verse frames the story with human honor in creating all earthly things for people and with God's knowledge, the story's two central pillars.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f5.anchor: هذه الآية التي سبقت بها قصة آدم بدأت بتكريم الإنسان:

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.claim: Successful vicegerency requires authority to administer its domain and proven capacity; God gave humanity the earth, Adam's test showed his fitness, and the chooser knows the unseen.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f10.anchor: أن يكون للخليفة حَقُّ التصرف والتدبير فيما استُخلِفَ فيه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.claim: The verse before the story summarizes both Adam's narrative and the two requirements of vicegerency: the earth is given to people and God knows everything.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r12/f11.anchor: أنَّ الآية التي وقعت في مقدمة القصة أجملت قصة آدم من ناحية، وأجملت ركني الاستخلاف المذكور فيها من ناحية أخرى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.claim: Al-Baqara's account centers on Adam's honor and the knowledge he bears; teaching Adam extends to his descendants' succession, which entails both the right and the ability to act, with ability established through knowledge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p800/r2.anchor: وهل هو قادر على القيام بالمهمة أو لا (أثبت القدرة بالعلم)

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.claim: The reasons for worship in 2:21–22 are paired with reasons against disbelief here: creation and provision are followed by life, death, resurrection, return, and creation of what is on earth, preparing for the account of human origins and stages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p373#2/r3.anchor: ومن بديع المناسبة وفائق التفنن في ضروب الانتقالات في المخاطبات أن كانت العلل التي قرن بها الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى
